title: `UnknownFieldAccess (9012)` remediation tells the operator to run a CLI command that is permanently broken (stub `discover` always exits 2)
userImpact: An LLM hits `UnknownFieldAccess (9012)` on a field write (the most common error during initial setup since the v1 base shards ship empty per FieldAccessMapLoader docs). The remediation says `'Run `lacerte-mcp field-access discover` to populate the map, or pass force:true to override.'` The operator runs `lacerte-mcp field-access discover` and it exits 2 with a stub message (FieldAccessCommand `discover` is documented in README line 269 as 'stub today; always exits 2'). The operator now thinks the install is broken OR re-runs it under elevated privileges OR files an issue — none of which fix the actual problem. The actual remediation is `pass force:true` or call `lacerte_field_access_map` to confirm the field is genuinely unmapped, or run `LacertMCP.FieldAccessDumper.exe` then `lacerte_reload_schema`.
description: Three independent surfaces collude to misdirect: (1) `SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:169` remediation names the broken stub command. (2) `FieldAccessMapLoader.cs:232` also stuffs `context['suggestedCli'] = 'lacerte-mcp field-access discover'` into every 9012 envelope, so even after the remediation string is fixed the context dict still points at the dead command. (3) README line 269 freely admits `discover` is `stub today; always exits 2` but no audit round connected the dots back to the remediation strings. The result: the canonical error → remediation chain leads the operator to a no-op command.
recommendation: Edit SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:169 remediation to: `'Call `lacerte_field_access_map(module, table, year)` to see what IS writable for this module/year, then either pick a mapped field or run `LacertMCP.FieldAccessDumper.exe` on a Windows + Lacerte box followed by `lacerte_reload_schema` to populate the map. Pass `force:true` to override the gate for one call (audit trail will note it).'` Also edit FieldAccessMapLoader.cs:232 to remove `suggestedCli` (or replace its value with the `lacerte_field_access_map` MCP tool call, which actually works in-session). Update README's `discover` subsection (line 269) to cross-reference the FieldAccessDumper workflow as the working alternative. This is the highest-leverage remediation-text fix because 9012 is the FIRST error a write-path operator typically encounters.
rationale: Round-1 P14-004 covered COM lifetime and round-2 P15-003 covered DECISIONS-md gaps for the access map — neither flagged that the remediation string for the most common write-time error points at a broken CLI verb. This is the single most actionable usability fix in the discoverability lens because it converts a dead-end UX into a productive one with three surfaces of text editing and zero code changes.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all three cited surfaces. SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:169 verbatim says 'Run `lacerte-mcp field-access discover` to populate the map, or pass force:true to override.' and FieldAccessMapLoader.cs:232 verbatim stuffs context['suggestedCli'] = 'lacerte-mcp field-access discover' into every 9012 envelope. README.md:269 still calls discover a 'stub today; always exits 2.' One factual correction to the finding: the discover stub now actually exits 3 (not 2) and already prints a redirect to LacertMCP.FieldAccessDumper.exe — that was fixed by Round-2 r2 finding #687 (P15-029 in the CLI). But the r2 fix touched only the CLI handler; it never updated the remediation string OR the suggestedCli context key. So today an LLM/operator hitting 9012 reads a 'do X' remediation, runs X, hits a different message telling them to actually use Y (the dumper). That double-redirect on the most common write-time error is a real usability fix and was not flagged in either prior round. The earlier r2 finding ~#1668 about reason-context duplication actually preserved the broken suggestedCli value in its recommendation — confirming this angle slipped through. Fix is sim-only, no Windows, ~3 string edits + 1 doc edit, and the proposed alternative path (lacerte_field_access_map MCP tool + lacerte_reload_schema MCP tool) genuinely exists today (MetadataTools.cs:17, SchemaReloadTools.cs:44), so the new remediation text would point at working tools the LLM can actually call mid-session.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Three-surface text fix, all sim-actionable, no Windows needed.

(1) SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:169 — replace the UnknownFieldAccess remediation string with: "Field is not in the access map (v1 base shards ship empty for many modules). To recover in-session: call `lacerte_field_access_map(module, table, year)` to see what IS writable for this module/table/year — if the field is genuinely supported but unmapped, pass `force:true` on the original call to override the gate (the override is audit-logged). To permanently populate the map: run `LacertMCP.FieldAccessDumper.exe --module <X> --table <N>` on a Windows + Lacerte box, then call the `lacerte_reload_schema` MCP tool so the new shards take effect without restarting the server (restart would invalidate the 24h Intuit auth ticket)." This converts a dead-end ("run the stub") into three concrete next steps an LLM can actually pick from based on context.

(2) FieldAccessMapLoader.cs:232 — delete `context["suggestedCli"] = "lacerte-mcp field-access discover";` and replace with `context["suggestedMcpTool"] = "lacerte_field_access_map";` (a working in-session call). The existing `context["suggestedRetryArgs"] = { force = true }` already covers the override path. Drop the dead CLI handle entirely — there is no working CLI verb to suggest at this seam.

(3) README.md:269 — replace "stub today; always exits 2. Bulk field-access introspection needs the live SDK; tracked as follow-up F5 in Todo.md." with "stub — always exits 3 and prints a redirect to `LacertMCP.FieldAccessDumper.exe` (the standalone introspector, ships under `src/LacertMCP.FieldAccessDumper/`). After running the dumper against a Windows + live Lacerte install, call the `lacerte_reload_schema` MCP tool from your LLM host so the new shards take effect without a server restart." This finally connects the three docs (CLI stub message, FieldAccessDumper, lacerte_reload_schema) into one coherent operator story.

(4) Add a 1-line regression test in the existing SyntheticStatusCodes tests asserting `StatusInfoFor(UnknownFieldAccess).Remediation.Contains("lacerte_field_access_map")` and `!Remediation.Contains("field-access discover")` so any future regression of the stale string fails CI. Same for a FieldAccessMapLoader test asserting the context dict does NOT carry a `suggestedCli` key for the Unknown branch.

title: Error envelope is missing the `origin` field that README, DECISIONS, and (implicitly) every LLM consumer expects
userImpact: Every error envelope shipped to Claude Desktop / Cursor is missing the documented `origin: "sdk" | "synthetic"` discriminator. The README's `## Errors` section, the example JSON, and the DECISIONS.md 2026-05-30 "Error envelope carries `origin` discriminator" entry all tell the LLM to expect an `origin` field — but `WrapToolHandler.SerializeError` builds an envelope with `{success, statusCode, statusName, severity, userMessage, remediation, context, cid}` and never sets `origin`. The LLM is told it can route remediation by reading `origin` but the field is silently absent, forcing fallback to range-based heuristics the docs explicitly tell it not to use.
description: Prior round 2 task P15-037 (audit-findings-r2.json:903) was supposed to add `["origin"] = err.StatusCode >= 9000 ? "synthetic" : "sdk"` to SerializeError. The docs half landed (README.md:184-210 introduces and documents `origin`; DECISIONS.md:331-369 has a full entry titled "Error envelope carries `origin` discriminator"; LacerteSDKError.cs:44 even exposes the `Origin` property). The serialization half did not — SerializeError's envelope dict has no `["origin"]` key. Code-vs-docs gap is exactly the bug the audit was meant to close.
recommendation: Add one line to SerializeError between `statusName` and `severity` (or anywhere before `cid`): `["origin"] = err.Origin,`. `LacerteSDKError.Origin` already returns the correct value. Then add a test in WrapToolHandlerTests asserting the envelope contains `"origin":"synthetic"` for SyntheticStatusCodes.SimulationOnly and `"origin":"sdk"` for StatusCodes.ExposedForRead.
rationale: P15-037 audit was confirmed, refinedRecommendation was specific ("add one field to the SerializeError envelope"), tests were specified. Only the docs half landed. Direct re-reading of WrapToolHandler.cs:144-158 confirms `origin` is still absent.

verdict.reasoning:
Direct file reads confirm every premise of the finding:

1. **Envelope is missing `origin`** — `src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/WrapToolHandler.cs:144-158` (`SerializeError`) builds a Dictionary with exactly {success, statusCode, statusName, severity, userMessage, remediation, context, cid} — no `origin` key. The XML doc on the class (lines 22-23) also lists the envelope fields and omits `origin`, so even the in-code contract is inconsistent with the published one.

2. **The property to read is already wired** — `src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/LacerteSDKError.cs:31-44` defines `public string Origin => StatusCode >= SyntheticCodeThreshold ? "synthetic" : "sdk";` with a full XML doc citing P15-037 and DECISIONS. The serializer just needs to read it.

3. **Docs ship the field as fact, not aspiration** — `README.md:184` says "see the `## Errors` section below for the full field list, semantics, and `origin` discriminator", and lines 190-210 show an example envelope literally containing `"origin": "synthetic"` plus prose explaining `sdk` vs `synthetic`. `DECISIONS.md:331-369` has a full dated entry "Error envelope carries `origin: "sdk" | "synthetic"` discriminator — P15-037" whose Downstream bullet explicitly states "`WrapToolHandler.SerializeError` reads `err.Origin` and emits it in the error envelope". Neither happened.

4. **No test guards this** — Grep across `src/LacertMCP.Tests/Errors/` (WrapToolHandlerTests.cs, WrapToolHandlerInternalErrorTests.cs, WrapToolHandlerRedactionTests.cs, LacerteSDKErrorTests.cs) finds zero envelope-side `origin` assertions. The single `origin` match in LacerteSDKErrorTests.cs:34 is an unrelated comment about TPSDKStatus codes. That's why this regression sat undetected — the property is unit-tested, the serializer path is not.

5. **Not a prior-round duplicate** — The original P15-037 (audit-findings-r2.json:903) had this exact refinedRecommendation ("add one field to the SerializeError envelope after `statusName`: `["origin"] = err.StatusCode >= 9000 ? "synthetic" : "sdk"`"). The docs half (README + DECISIONS) landed; the envelope half did not. This is a NEW finding under round 3 because the prior task was marked done after only partial completion. The cross-tool `lacerte_return_codes` catalog tool (MetadataTools.cs) already emits `origin` per code, so the LLM sees `origin` in the catalog response, expects it in error envelopes too, and silently doesn't get it.

**Why it meaningfully improves UX (not bikeshedding):** Two real moments degrade today. (a) An LLM that read the README or called `lacerte_return_codes` first will write client code that conditionals on `envelope.origin === "synthetic"` to know whether to retry-with-different-args vs surface-to-operator. Today that condition is always false (undefined), so retry logic silently misroutes. (b) When an operator pastes a Claude Desktop error transcript into a bug report, the documented "tell me the origin" step the README implies fails. The fix is one line in SerializeError + 2-3 tests, fully sim-doable, ~10 minutes. The user-visible outcome is exactly the LLM-routing experience the round-2 audit committed to delivering.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Three small, sim-only changes (~10 min total):

(1) **`src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/WrapToolHandler.cs:144-158`** — add one entry to the `SerializeError` envelope dict between `statusName` and `severity`:
```csharp
["statusName"] = err.StatusName,
["origin"] = err.Origin,            // <-- add
["severity"] = err.Severity.ToString().ToLowerInvariant(),
```
Use `err.Origin` (not an inline `StatusCode >= 9000` ternary) because the property already exists on `LacerteSDKError` with the canonical threshold constant `SyntheticCodeThreshold = 9000` — keeps the rule in one place if it ever moves.

(2) **Also fix the class XML doc** on `WrapToolHandler` (line 22-23) so the in-code contract matches: `{ "success": false, "statusCode", "statusName", "origin", "severity", "userMessage", "remediation", "context", "cid" }`. Otherwise the next contributor reading the docstring will see the old shape.

(3) **Add tests in `src/LacertMCP.Tests/Errors/WrapToolHandlerTests.cs`** (file exists). Three assertions, parse the returned JSON and check the `origin` property:
 - throw `new LacerteSDKError(SyntheticStatusCodes.SimulationOnly)` → envelope `"origin":"synthetic"`
 - throw `new LacerteSDKError(StatusCodes.ExposedForRead /*8*/)` → envelope `"origin":"sdk"`
 - throw generic `InvalidOperationException` (routes through the catch-all that wraps as SyntheticStatusCodes.InternalServerError 9203) → envelope `"origin":"synthetic"` (this also nails down the post-P15-035 generic-exception path).

No doc edits needed in README/DECISIONS — they already describe the intended behavior; this PR just lands the code half of P15-037 as committed.

title: Three docs publish wrong test count (695/705) while HANDOFF says 1006/1016 — top-of-funnel trust killer
userImpact: An operator (or a future contributor) reading README's Status line sees "695/705 tests passing" and runs `dotnet test`, gets 1006 passing, and now distrusts every other claim in the README. REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md says "reports 695 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed" as a Verify step — so anyone who actually completes the regression list as written will mark it failed because the number doesn't match. HANDOFF.md line 39 explicitly claims "Round-2 docs sync — README/REGRESSION_CHECKLIST/HANDOFF test counts updated to current" but that work didn't land in those two files.
description: README.md:5: "v0.1.0 scaffolding — 695/705 tests passing (10 expected live-only skips)". REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:13: "reports 695 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed". Actual: HANDOFF.md:19 says 1006/1016 (and Phase-15 round-2 grew it to that). Round 2 docs-sync claim is self-falsifying.
recommendation: Update README.md:5 to "1006/1016 tests passing" and REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:13 to "1006 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed". Also remove the brittle hard-coded number from README's Status line in favor of "all suites passing" + a link to HANDOFF for the current count, so the number lives in exactly one place.
rationale: Verified by reading both files. The 695 number lived through both audit rounds despite an explicit P15-001 task ('Stale test counts in REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md + README.md after 695-test jump') being marked done in Todo.md:514. The fix didn't actually catch the round-2 +311 delta.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading the cited lines. README.md:5 literally says "695/705 tests passing (10 expected live-only skips)" and REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:13 literally says "reports **695 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed**". HANDOFF.md:19 and :50 explicitly say "1006/1016 tests passing" / "must report **1006 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed**". HANDOFF.md:39 self-falsifies by claiming "Round-2 docs sync — README/REGRESSION_CHECKLIST/HANDOFF test counts updated to current". Prior P15-001 (Todo.md:514) addressed the 481 to 695 jump but did NOT catch the round-2 695 to 1006 jump in these two files — so this is a NEW slip from round 2's own promised work, not a duplicate of P15-001. It's a real round-3 usability finding: anyone running the regression checklist literally as written marks the gate failed when their `dotnet test` shows 1006 instead of 695, eroding trust in every other documented number. The fix-forward (collapse to "all suites passing" + link HANDOFF as the single source of truth, mirroring the tool-count pattern REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:20 already established) is the right shape to prevent the same drift from recurring.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Two surgical edits plus one anti-drift change: (1) README.md:5 — replace "695/705 tests passing (10 expected live-only skips), 0 failures, 0 warnings" with "all suites passing, 0 failures, 0 warnings — see HANDOFF.md for current counts". This kills the hard-coded number at the top-of-funnel doc so it can't go stale again. (2) REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:13 — replace "**695 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed**" with "**1006 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed** (count drifts as tests land; the operative check is 0 failed + skip count stable at 10)". Frames the test count as a trend signal, not an exact match, so a future +N test addition doesn't re-break the checklist. (3) Optionally add a one-line note to HANDOFF.md:39's docs-sync bullet pointing to this round-3 catch as evidence the count-as-checklist-value pattern is brittle, and recommend future agents always soften test-count assertions to "0 failed, 10 skipped" wherever they appear (the failure/skip counts are stable; the pass count is not).

title: README troubleshooting cites two non-existent error codes (`NotSignedIn 9101`, `TicketExpired 9103`) that operators will never see in the wire
userImpact: When an operator's 24h ticket expires and they grep the README for the error code they actually got, they find nothing. README troubleshooting tells them to expect `NotSignedIn (9101)` or `TicketExpired (9103)`. The actual production code throws either raw `NotSignedIn (203)` (SDK code) or synthetic `LoginExpired (9007)`. Code 9101 (`ReAuthRequired`) is defined but never thrown by anything in production. Code 9103 is `InvalidAppId`, NOT `TicketExpired` — and `TicketExpired` is a status name that doesn't exist in SyntheticStatusCodes at all. So the wire fingerprint the README documents simply cannot occur; the troubleshooting section is unreachable.
description: Grep across .md files shows ARCHITECTURE.md lines 34/62/79/111 all describe expiry as "synth 9101 with remediation". README.md:291 escalates by naming `TicketExpired (9103)` — but SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:87 defines 9103 as `InvalidAppId` (P15-007). The only code actually thrown on expiry is `LoginExpired (9007)` per LacerteSessionManager.cs:1369 (`ThrowIfAuthExpired`). And LoginCommand.cs:74 prints to operator stderr: "tools will return TicketExpired (9103) once the current ticket lapses" — also wrong, will mislead anyone trying to triage.
recommendation: Either (a) wire `ReAuthRequired (9101)` actually into ThrowIfAuthExpired and the AutoReconnect NotSignedIn path so the docs become true, or (b) rewrite all five doc/code sites to say `LoginExpired (9007)` and `NotSignedIn (203 sdk)` — which is what really fires. Option (b) is the smaller change. Also delete the `TicketExpired (9103)` reference everywhere it appears (no such name exists). After the fix, run `grep -nE "9101|9103|TicketExpired"` across .md and CLI commands and confirm only intended results remain.
rationale: Cross-checked SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:27-102 (codes 9007=LoginExpired, 9101=ReAuthRequired-never-thrown, 9103=InvalidAppId) against LacerteSessionManager.cs:1364-1369 (ThrowIfAuthExpired throws LoginExpired). No throw site for 9101 in production code (only in tests at LacerteSDKErrorTests.cs:51). `TicketExpired` is not a defined symbol anywhere.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified all five cited sites. The drift is real and induced by prior round-2 work, never reconciled:

(1) README.md:291 — Says expired sessions surface as `NotSignedIn (9101)` or `TicketExpired (9103)`. Wrong on both counts: `NotSignedIn` is SDK code 203 (not 9101); 9101 is `ReAuthRequired` and is NEVER thrown in production (Grep across src finds only one use, in LacerteSDKErrorTests.cs:51). `TicketExpired` is not a defined StatusInfo name anywhere — 9103 is `InvalidAppId` per SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:87/201, the slot allocated by P15-007 to fix the mis-categorized AppNotRegistered throw. The actual production code thrown on 24h expiry is `LoginExpired (9007)` per LacerteSessionManager.cs:1369 ThrowIfAuthExpired (wired by P15-043).

(2) LoginCommand.cs:74 — Prints to operator stderr: 'tools will return TicketExpired (9103) once the current ticket lapses'. This string was implanted verbatim by the P15-028 round-2 refinedRecommendation (audit-findings-r2.json:681), which suggested the wording before P15-007 had finalized 9103=InvalidAppId. The two round-2 verdicts collided and no doc-reconciliation pass caught it.

(3) ARCHITECTURE.md lines 34, 62, 79, 111 — All four describe expiry remediation as 'synth 9101'. Line 111 says 'every tool call short-circuits to synthetic 9101 with remediation pointing to lacerte-mcp login'. Line 79 (Boundary Invariant #8) makes the same claim. Production wires `LoginExpired (9007)` for the proactive probe; the reactive NotSignedIn path through AutoReconnect.cs explicitly propagates unchanged (line 194: 'LacerteSDKError carries a TAPIStatus — those are NEVER transient'), so an operator hitting reactive expiry sees raw SDK code 203, never 9101.

(4) REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:126 — Asserts 'every tool call short-circuits to synthetic 9101 ReAuthRequired with the lacerte-mcp login remediation message'. This is a regression test the operator can never pass because nothing throws 9101.

Not a duplicate of prior rounds: P15-007 added 9103=InvalidAppId (didn't audit existing 9103 mentions). P15-028 added the LoginCommand stderr line (using the now-wrong code). P15-043 wired LoginExpired=9007 as the actual expiry throw site (didn't update the docs that still cited 9101). The integration gap between the three is what this finding catches.

User-experience cost is concrete: a tax pro at 9am the next day sees `{statusCode: 9007, statusName: "LoginExpired"}` in the wire, greps the README for '9007' (finds nothing), then for 'LoginExpired' (finds nothing in README), then reads the troubleshooting section verbatim and is told to expect a code they're not seeing. Trust in docs erodes; triage time grows. LLM clients have the same problem — Claude Desktop showing 9007 to the model while the README it's been pointed at advertises 9101/9103 makes the LLM less likely to map to the correct remediation.

Recommendation is small and high-leverage (option b in the finding): five edits to align docs with what actually fires. Sim-only, no Lacerte SDK needed, can be locked with a single regression test that greps the .md files for the right symbols.

Slight over-statement in the finding: 9101 and 9103 ARE defined constants, just not what the docs imply. But the user impact is identical — operators searching for codes they actually see will not find a match.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Single pass to reconcile docs with the codes that actually fire. Five edits + one regression test.

(1) README.md:289-293 — Rewrite the symptom + diagnosis block to:
'**Symptom:** Reads + writes that worked yesterday now fail with status `LoginExpired (9007)` (proactive probe) or raw SDK `NotSignedIn (203)` (if the reactive NotSignedIn slips past the probe). Both error envelopes include the remediation `Run lacerte_register to re-authenticate (consent is one-time; only the sign-in needs refresh).`'
This makes the README the canonical fingerprint that matches what operators actually see in tool envelopes.

(2) LoginCommand.cs:74 — Change the stderr line to:
`Console.Error.WriteLine("          Existing 24h ticket cannot be renewed until upgrade — tools will return LoginExpired (9007) once the current ticket lapses.");`
Mirror the same correction in the comment at line 71.

(3) ARCHITECTURE.md:111 — Change 'short-circuits to synthetic 9101' to 'short-circuits to synthetic 9007 (LoginExpired) via the ThrowIfAuthExpired probe in LacerteSessionManager'. Cross-reference DECISIONS.md if a 'Auth expiry surfacing code' entry exists; if not, add one.

(4) ARCHITECTURE.md:34 — Update the diagram comment `- Idempotency cache (synth 9101 reuse)` — this is wrong twice over. 9101 isn't idempotency, 9102 is (IdempotencyConflict). Fix to: `- Idempotency cache (synth 9102 conflict)`.

(5) ARCHITECTURE.md:62 + :79 — Both reference '9101' in the resilience / Boundary Invariant #8 context. Change 9101 to '9007 (proactive probe) and raw 203 NotSignedIn (reactive path; AutoReconnect propagates unchanged per Resilience/AutoReconnect.cs:194)'. The invariant text should be honest that the reactive path is currently raw.

(6) REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:126 — Change to: 'After 24h elapse OR explicit logout: every tool call that touches RequireContext short-circuits to synthetic 9007 LoginExpired with the `lacerte_register` remediation message; calls that bypass RequireContext (e.g. lacerte_session_status) still succeed and report registered:false.' This matches the actual P15-043 implementation.

(7) Decide what to do with 9101 ReAuthRequired (currently a dead constant). Two options:
  (a) Delete it from SyntheticStatusCodes.cs + StatusTable + LacerteSDKErrorTests.cs:51 — it's a docs-promised behavior that was never built and no longer planned (9007 covers the use case).
  (b) Wire it into AutoReconnect's NotSignedIn detection path so the reactive case finally surfaces a friendly code instead of raw 203. This is more work but closes Boundary Invariant #8 honestly. The P15-043 verdict explicitly suggested this as a follow-up.
Recommend (a) for this round; track (b) as a separate Todo. Reasoning: a dead constant that docs falsely reference is worse than no constant — operators reading SyntheticStatusCodes.cs will see 9101 ReAuthRequired and assume something throws it.

(8) Regression test — add `src/LacertMCP.Tests/Docs/StatusCodeDocsAlignmentTests.cs` with one test per doc file:
- Asserts README.md does NOT contain the substrings `9101`, `9103`, or `TicketExpired` (after the fix, these strings must not appear because they're wrong or refer to InvalidAppId which is not an auth-lifecycle thing).
- Asserts ARCHITECTURE.md does NOT contain `9101` (after delete + fix).
- Asserts REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md does NOT contain `9101 ReAuthRequired`.
- Asserts LoginCommand.cs does NOT contain `TicketExpired`.
- Asserts the codes that DO appear in StatusInfo.cs StatusTable are referenced at least once in README.md (catches future drift the other direction).

Verify with `Grep -nE "9101|9103|TicketExpired|ReAuthRequired" --glob "*.md"` post-edit; only the SyntheticStatusCodes.cs definition of 9103=InvalidAppId should remain (and only if option (a) above is chosen, no 9101 anywhere).

title: README has zero sim-mode MCP host config example, blocking the no-Lacerte tryout path
userImpact: A first-time user (or LLM walking the README in Claude Desktop) cannot connect the MCP in simulation mode without hand-crafting an env block. The only `mcpServers` JSON example sets `LACERTE_LIVE=1` + a real `LACERTE_DATA_PATH`. The 'For dev / sim against the source tree' line says only 'swap path X for path Y' without telling the reader to also remove `LACERTE_LIVE=1` and add `LACERTE_SIMULATION=1`.
description: README §'Install paths (per MCP client)' only ships one Claude Desktop / generic MCP host JSON example, and it is the LIVE-mode flavour aimed at the production operator. There is no copy-pasteable 'Try the sim seed on a fresh checkout — no Lacerte needed' block. Combined with the existing seeded fixture (SeedData.cs: SMIT, JONE, REJE, BROW, PEND, ACME, WIDG, PART across TY20 IData, TY24 IData, TY24 CData, TY24 PData), this is a documentation gap, not a code gap: the demoable experience exists but cannot be invoked through the documented path. An LLM host opening the README sees only a config that requires Lacerte installed plus a registered AppID.
recommendation: Add a second JSON block under §'Claude Desktop' labelled 'Sim mode (no Lacerte install required — uses the in-memory 8-client seed)' with `LACERTE_SIMULATION=1`, no `LACERTE_LIVE`, no `LACERTE_DATA_PATH`. Below it, list the 4 seeded datapaths (e.g. 'try lacerte_set_context dataPath=C:\Lacerte\24Tax\IData taxYear=2024 module=I to see BROW + PEND') so the LLM has a concrete first call. Also fix the 'swap path X for path Y' sentence to spell out the env-var diff (remove LACERTE_LIVE=1, add LACERTE_SIMULATION=1).
rationale: Prior rounds focused on correctness/architecture/redaction split. They did not audit the first-five-minutes path for an operator who just wants to confirm the wiring works before touching Lacerte. The SeedData fixture is the killer demo and the README never tells anyone it exists.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading README.md:46-83 directly. The only Claude Desktop / generic-stdio JSON example is the LIVE-mode flavor (LACERTE_LIVE=1, LACERTE_DATA_PATH=C:\\Lacerte\\24data, LACERTE_APP_NAME, LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE). The single line bridging to sim mode (line 69: 'For dev / sim against the source tree, swap C:\\\\LacertMCP\\\\server\\\\LacertMCP.Server.exe for C:\\\\path\\\\to\\\\LacertMCP\\\\src\\\\...') tells the reader to swap the binary path but is silent on the env-block diff — it doesn't say to drop LACERTE_LIVE=1 or add LACERTE_SIMULATION=1. title: Seeded sim fixture is invisible to operators and LLMs — SMIT/JONE/ACME/PART are documented only in C# source
userImpact: On a fresh checkout the operator builds, points Claude Desktop at the sim server, and asks Claude 'list my clients' — Claude calls `lacerte_client_list` and gets a `ContextNotSet` error. To unstick this, Claude would need to call `lacerte_list_datapaths`, but off-Windows that returns `{ datapaths: [] }` (the C:\Lacerte tree doesn't exist on the dev box). The 4 canonical seeded datapaths (DataPathIData2020/2024, DataPathCData2024, DataPathPData2024) are documented only inside SeedData.cs as `public const string`. There is no way for an LLM consumer to discover them. The first interaction therefore produces a dead-end error.
description: The sim store seeds 8 clients across 3 modules and 2 years (per SeedData.cs class-doc table at L14-22). These are documented in `docs/research/agents/06-simulation-mode.md §2` and SeedData.cs but nowhere a user of the assembled product would see — not in the README, not in `lacerte-mcp tools`, not surfaced by `lacerte_list_datapaths` (which scans the filesystem, not the sim store), and not in the `lacerte_health` response. The 'two-mode discipline' invariant in CLAUDE.md says sim and live must be observationally identical — but in sim mode there is no real Lacerte install, so `lacerte_list_datapaths` returns an empty list and the seeded sim paths are unreachable through the documented discovery flow.
recommendation: Two complementary fixes. (a) In `LacerteListDatapaths`, when running in simulation mode, return the canonical sim datapaths (the 4 `SeedData.DataPathXxx` constants) alongside any filesystem hits, with a `source: 'sim-seed'` discriminator on each row so live/sim parity is preserved at the schema level. (b) Add a README subsection §'Seeded simulation data' immediately after Quick start with a table mirroring the SeedData class-doc — paths, years, modules, and ClientNumbers (SMIT=1001, JONE=1002, REJE=1003, BROW=1001/TY24, PEND=1002/TY24, ACME=1001/CData, etc.) so an LLM picking up the README can paste-quote them into its first `lacerte_set_context` call.
rationale: Round-2 P15-009/P15-010/P15-072 polished read-tool ergonomics but never closed the discovery loop in sim mode. This is the single biggest 'first call works' usability win.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified end-to-end by direct file reads. Every claim in the finding holds up:

(1) **SeedData.cs L14-22 confirmed** — `public const string DataPathIData2020/2024, DataPathCData2024, DataPathPData2024` (lines 29-32) plus 8 seeded clients (SMIT/JONE/REJE/BROW/PEND/ACME/WIDG/PART) with specific ClientNumbers are only visible inside the C# source. The class-doc Roster table is there too, but only at lines 14-22 — invisible to any operator or LLM consuming the assembled product.

(2) **`LacerteListDatapaths` is filesystem-only** — SessionTools.cs:143-156 calls `DiscoverDatapaths(root)` which `return result;` immediately when `!Directory.Exists(root)` (line 172). Off-Windows the response is `{root: "C:\\Lacerte", rootExists: false, count: 0, datapaths: []}`. Zero sim-store awareness.

(3) **README has no seeded-sim section** — env table at L87-101 mentions `LACERTE_DATA_ROOT` but nowhere lists the canonical seeded paths/IDs. The "Quick start (dev / simulation mode)" section walks through build/test/CLI but never tells the operator what clients/paths exist to play with.

(4) **The damage is operationally real** — `WorkflowPrompts.ClientIntake` (Prompts/WorkflowPrompts.cs:55) explicitly tells the LLM: "If `context` is null, call `lacerte_list_datapaths` to discover available installs." In sim mode this returns empty, and the prompt has no fallback branch — the LLM is dead-stuck.

(5) **`lacerte_health` doesn't help** — HealthTools.cs:39 returns only `{mode, status, heartbeatPath?}` — no roster, no seeded paths.

(6) **Not a duplicate of prior P14/P15 work** — Searched both audit files for sim-datapath discovery, seeded roster surfacing, or list_datapaths sim parity. Closest hits:
   - P14-016/P14-033 added `LACERTE_DATA_ROOT` to README env table — addresses live mode discovery only.
   - P15-009 — detail-read series filter (different surface).
   - P15-010 — EF status filter (different surface).
   - P15-072 — wire-log payload summarization (different surface).
   None close this loop.

(7) **The "two-mode discipline" tension noted in the finding is correctly identified** — CLAUDE.md `## Two-mode discipline` says sim and live must be observationally identical, yet `list_datapaths` returns empty in sim because there's no real install. The fix (return seeded paths with a `source: "sim-seed"` discriminator) preserves the invariant at the schema level — the column shape stays the same, just with a provenance tag.

This is the highest-leverage "first call works" usability win the prior 149 fixes left on the table. The fix is fully in-session actionable, sim-only, ~30 LoC + a README table. Severity is "high" because every fresh checkout fails the operator's first interaction — and the operator profile is a tax pro on Windows who has just plugged Claude Desktop into the server and asked "show me my clients."
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Composite fix, all sim-only, in-session actionable.

**(A) Surface seeded sim datapaths through `lacerte_list_datapaths`** (the load-bearing piece — closes the prompt's dead-end branch):

In `SessionTools.LacerteListDatapaths` (src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/SessionTools.cs:143-156), after computing filesystem `entries`, check whether the active session is in sim mode. If so, merge the 4 canonical seeded paths from `SeedData.DataPathXxx` (already public const). Add a `source` field to every row in the response (`"filesystem"` or `"sim-seed"`) so live and sim stay observationally identical at the schema level — a tool can still tell modes apart only by reading `source`, and the column shape never changes. Bonus: when running in sim mode, also include `clientCount` per row so the LLM can see "IData/2024 → 2 clients" at a glance.

Concrete dispatch:
- The class today takes no session dependency. The cleanest path is to add `LacerteSessionManager session` to the ctor (matching `HealthTools`/`ClientsTools` pattern) and ask `session.IsSimulationMode` (or whatever the boolean predicate is — `SessionStatusSnapshot.mode == "simulation"`).
- For each `SeedData.DataPath*` constant in sim mode: emit `{ path, year, module, moduleName, source: "sim-seed", clientCount: <count> }` and tag every filesystem hit with `source: "filesystem"`.
- Deduplicate by `(path, year, module)` so a live operator with `LACERTE_DATA_ROOT` overriding to a tree that happens to contain a `20Tax\IData` folder isn't double-listed (filesystem source wins).

Add one parity test: `ListDatapaths_InSim_ReturnsCanonicalSeededPaths` asserting the 4 canonical paths are present and tagged `sim-seed` when no live install exists; and a live-mode test asserting the response excludes `sim-seed` rows.

**(B) Add a `### Seeded simulation data` subsection to README** immediately after "Quick start (dev / simulation mode)" (after line 44, before "Install paths"). Mirror the SeedData class-doc table verbatim so the LLM picking up the README on first interaction can paste-quote the values into `lacerte_set_context`:

```
### Seeded simulation data

When running in simulation mode (default off-Windows), the in-memory store ships with 8 canonical clients across 3 modules and 2 tax years. Use these for first-touch verification before pointing at a real Lacerte install:

| Datapath | Year | Module | Clients (ClientID → ClientNumber) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `C:\Lacerte\20Tax\IData` | 2020 | I | SMIT→1001 (single), JONE→1002 (joint+1 dep), REJE→1003 (EF rejected) |
| `C:\Lacerte\24Tax\IData` | 2024 | I | BROW→1001 (joint+2 deps), PEND→1002 (EF Transmitted) |
| `C:\Lacerte\24Tax\CData` | 2024 | C | ACME→1001 (1120, CA+NY), WIDG→1002 (1120, TX) |
| `C:\Lacerte\24Tax\PData` | 2024 | P | PART→1001 (1065, 3 partners via DATA2 subclients) |

These are emitted by `lacerte_list_datapaths` with `source: "sim-seed"`. The datapath strings are literal — pass them verbatim to `lacerte_set_context`.
```

**(C) Update `lacerte_client_intake` prompt** (Prompts/WorkflowPrompts.cs:55) to mention the sim-seed fallback in one extra sentence so an LLM that gets an empty `datapaths` list off-Windows isn't stuck: "If the response is empty AND you're in simulation mode (per `lacerte_health.mode`), the simulation store provides 4 canonical seeded datapaths — also documented in the README 'Seeded simulation data' table." After (A) ships this becomes belt-and-braces — `list_datapaths` will already return the sim-seed rows — but it future-proofs the prompt against the LLM ignoring the `source` field.

**(D) Optional polish** — Add the 4 canonical sim datapaths + client counts to the `lacerte_health` response under a `sim` subkey when `mode == "simulation"`. Shape: `{ mode: "simulation", status: "reachable", sim: { seeded: [{path, year, module, clientCount}, ...] } }`. This gives the LLM a second discovery surface that doesn't even require calling `list_datapaths`. Skip if it feels like overlap with (A); the (A) fix alone closes the dead-end.

**Skip** the audit's suggestion to also list every seeded ClientID in the README inline next to each datapath — the table form in (B) is cleaner. The ClientNumbers (1001/1002/1003) are also obvious from the seed (`NextClientNumber = N+1`) so don't sprinkle them through the prose; the table carries them once and that's enough.

Tests to add (~50 LoC total):
- `SessionToolsTests.ListDatapaths_InSim_IncludesSeedRowsWithSource`
- `SessionToolsTests.ListDatapaths_InLive_OmitsSeedRows` (guarded by `[FactWindowsOnly]` or via a fake mode predicate)
- `SessionToolsTests.ListDatapaths_DedupsFilesystemOverSimSeed` — sim mode + a temp dir matching the canonical path, assert one row tagged `filesystem`, not two.

This is the single highest-leverage "first call works" win for a fresh-checkout operator. Land it before any further read-tool ergonomics.

title: Mojibake (â€“ / Â§) baked into LLM-visible tool [Description] strings in FieldWriteBulkTools
userImpact: When Claude Desktop / Cursor / Windsurf list the lacerte_field_write_bulk tool or read its parameter descriptions, the LLM sees garbled glyphs like 'JSON-serializable scalar â€" string, number, or boolean' and 'spec Â§2' instead of the intended em-dashes and § sign. This visibly erodes operator trust the first time they inspect the tool catalog, and the corrupted bytes also flow into Claude's context window where they consume extra tokens and can subtly degrade the model's parsing of the surrounding sentence.
description: The source file is saved as UTF-8 (verified with `file`), but at some point an editor saved Windows-1252 bytes (0x97 em-dash, 0xA7 section sign) as if they were UTF-8, producing the classic mojibake. Eight [Description]/<summary> strings are affected, and they are baked into the compiled assembly (the .exe file matches the same byte pattern), so this ships to operators every build. No other Server source file has this corruption — grep for the same byte sequences across the tree returns only FieldWriteBulkTools.cs. R2 audit P15-065 covered Doctor CLI glyph mojibake but did not touch tool descriptions.
recommendation: Open the file in an editor that explicitly reads as UTF-8, fix the four mangled em-dashes (`â€"` → `—` on lines 29, 66, 77 (two), 81, 82, 183) and one section sign (`Â§` → `§` on lines 17, 79), and save back as UTF-8 (no BOM is fine for .cs in net48 toolchain). Add a one-line grep guard to REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md (e.g. `grep -rl 'â€\|Â§\|Ã©' src/` must return empty) so the next contributor catches a recurrence before commit. Verify the fix by rebuilding and inspecting the .exe with `strings` (the bytes should now be `\xe2\x80\x94` UTF-8, not `\xc3\xa2\xe2\x82\xac"`).
rationale: Distinct from R2's DoctorCommand glyph finding — that one was about console-encoding rendering, this one is about the source bytes themselves being wrong. Pure cosmetic but high-visibility: every LLM that calls this MCP sees the corruption in the tool listing prompt and reads it back into its reasoning. Trivial in-session fix with a permanent guardrail.

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly by reading C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/FieldWriteBulkTools.cs. The file is UTF-8 (per `file` command) and contains 8 mojibake sequences at exactly the lines claimed: `Â§` on line 17 ('REQUIREMENTS Â§1.2'), four `â€"` on line 29 ('every row â€" NOT past it into ApplySimFieldWrite â€"'), one `â€"` on line 66 (Value [Description]), two `â€"` on line 77 inside the main tool's [Description] string (which is what Claude/Cursor/Windsurf show in the tool catalog), `Â§` on line 79 ('spec Â§2'), `â€"` on lines 81 + 82 (year + readOnly param [Description]s), and `â€"` on line 183 (xmldoc). Crucially, lines 66/77/79/81/82 are inside [Description] attributes that the MCP framework serializes to the LLM at tool-list time — this is genuinely LLM-visible. A grep across src/ confirms only this one file is corrupted (the same bytes appear in every built .exe, confirming they ship). Distinct from R2's P15-065 finding which was about DoctorCommand console codepage rendering — that's runtime stdout encoding, this is source-file bytes that bypass any console layer entirely. Phase-14 P15-008 introduced this file (the bulk-write tool) and the corruption shipped with it. Meaningfully improves: the operator's first inspection of `lacerte_field_write_bulk` in Claude Desktop's tool catalog shows visibly garbled punctuation — exactly the kind of first-impression trust signal that matters for a personal-tool operator who has the option to delete the MCP and write a Python script instead. Token impact is real but minor (each `â€"` is 3 bytes vs 3 for `—`, but tokenizers split mojibake into more sub-tokens than clean em-dashes, costing ~3-5 extra tokens per occurrence × 8 occurrences × every session). Trivial single-session fix.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Fix the 8 mojibake sequences in src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/FieldWriteBulkTools.cs by replacing every `â€"` (bytes c3 a2 e2 82 ac 22) with `—` (U+2014 em-dash, UTF-8 e2 80 94) and every `Â§` (bytes c2 a7 read as UTF-8 sequence c3 82 c2 a7) with `§` (U+00A7, UTF-8 c2 a7). Concretely: line 17 'REQUIREMENTS Â§1.2' → '§1.2'; line 29 two occurrences in 'every row â€" NOT past it into ApplySimFieldWrite â€"'; line 66 Value description 'JSON-serializable scalar â€" string, number, or boolean'; line 77 two occurrences inside the main tool [Description] ('idempotencyKey is supplied it acts as a prefix â€"'); line 79 'spec Â§2'; line 81 year param 'Optional â€"'; line 82 readOnly param 'Optional â€"'; line 183 xmldoc 'no idempotency â€"'. Save as UTF-8 (with or without BOM — net48 + Roslyn handle both; existing file is without BOM, keep consistent). After the edit, rebuild and grep the resulting .exe to confirm bytes are now `e2 80 94` not `c3 a2 e2 82 ac 22`. Add a guardrail line to REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md under the build/lint section: a literal mojibake grep that must return empty across src/ (something like: search src/ for the byte patterns `â€` and `Â§`, expect zero matches). This is a one-edit fix that takes under 5 minutes, eliminates a trust-eroding artifact every LLM session sees in the bulk-write tool catalog entry, and the checklist line prevents recurrence the next time a contributor copy-pastes a description from a Word doc or Outlook draft. Optional but cheap: skim every other Tools/*.cs file for stray `â€` or `Â` bytes in the same session (the grep already confirmed only this one file is affected today, but the checklist line should still cover all of src/).

title: `LacerteDetailWrite` has 11 required string parameters in fixed order — easy to misorder, no way to skip empties
userImpact: LLMs invoking this tool routinely pass arguments by name in most MCP clients, but when they pass positionally (or when the LLM forgets a middle string and shifts everything left) the silent result is a row with `source=""`, `tsj="W2"`, `importSrc="T"` — the validation only rejects empty Series/Code/bad State/bad TSJ. A misaligned `tsj="W2"` slips past TSJ validation if the operator typo'd. Even when passed by name, the LLM has to mentally construct 6+ empty strings (`prefix:"", suffix:"", stateAbbr:"", cityAbbr:"", source:"", tsj:"", importSrc:""`) for the common W-2 case, doubling the token cost and the chance of typo.
description: Signature: `(clientNumber, series, prefix, code, suffix, stateAbbr, cityAbbr, source, tsj, importSrc, amount, description, replaceIndex?, dryRun?, idempotencyKey?)`. Of the 12 required positionals, 7 (prefix, suffix, stateAbbr, cityAbbr, source, tsj, importSrc) are flagged in their own descriptions as 'often empty'. They all collapse to `""` server-side via `?? ""`. The descriptions say 'often empty' but the parameter is still required, forcing the LLM to invent the empty string.
recommendation: Default every 'often empty' string to `""`: change `string prefix` -> `string prefix = ""`, same for `suffix`, `stateAbbr`, `cityAbbr`, `source`, `tsj`, `importSrc`. Keep `series`, `code`, `clientNumber`, `description`, `amount` required (those are load-bearing). Result: a W-2 write goes from 12-arg invocation to `(clientNumber, series, code, amount, description)` — 5 args. This is purely additive to the schema (existing callers still pass them) and immediately cuts the LLM's mental model for the common case in half.
rationale: Round 1 P14-053 fixed `CreateClient`'s required-set vs spec mismatch but did not look at DetailWrite's positional ergonomics. No prior round examined parameter-ordering and default-value friction.

verdict.reasoning:
Direct read of DetailsTools.cs:100-117 confirms `LacerteDetailWrite` declares 12 required positionals, of which 7 (`prefix`, `suffix`, `stateAbbr`, `cityAbbr`, `source`, `tsj`, `importSrc`) are documented as 'often empty' in their own descriptions and silently coerced to `""` via `?? ""`. Test fixtures (e.g., `new DetailRow("X", "", "1", "", "", "", "", "", "", 1.0, "")` in SimulationStoreTests.cs:422,432,442,629 and DetailWriteRoundTripTests.cs) confirm the empty-string parade is endemic.

Novelty check: P14-053 (round 1) addressed `CreateClient`'s required-set vs spec mismatch but went the *opposite* direction (made nullable params required). No prior finding in rounds 1-2 touches DetailWrite's parameter-default ergonomics, the W-2 happy-path token cost, or the cross-tool inconsistency.

Cross-tool comparison strengthens the case: `LacerteFieldWrite` (FieldWriteTools.cs:47-48) already uses `string? = null` defaults for optional discriminators like `subClientID`, `stateAbbrev`. `LacerteClientCreate` and `LacerteDetailWrite` are the two outliers that force empty strings — and CreateClient was deliberately tightened by P14-053, leaving DetailWrite as the only tool that asks the LLM to invent 7 empty strings per common-case call.

One caveat on the finding's framing: the 'positional misordering' angle is somewhat overstated because MCP wire calls are JSON object-shaped, not positional — so an LLM literally cannot 'shift everything left'. The real wins are (a) cutting the W-2 invocation from 12 args to 5 in the schema the LLM emits, saving ~30-50 output tokens per call and removing 7 opportunities for the LLM to typo an empty-quoted string into a non-empty value, and (b) restoring cross-tool consistency with FieldWrite's default pattern. The fix is purely additive (existing tests and CLI sites still pass values explicitly), in-session, and lands as ~10 lines of diff in DetailsTools.cs.

This is a genuine LLM-UX win on the hottest write path in the API (DetailWrite is how every W-2, 1099, Schedule K-1 row gets entered), not bikeshedding.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Make the seven 'often empty' string params default to `""` in `DetailsTools.LacerteDetailWrite` (DetailsTools.cs:105-112), and rewrite their [Description] strings to make the default explicit so the LLM knows it can omit them. Concrete diff:

1. **Signature change** in `src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/DetailsTools.cs:102-117`:
   - `string prefix` -> `string prefix = ""`
   - `string suffix` -> `string suffix = ""`
   - `string stateAbbr` -> `string stateAbbr = ""`
   - `string cityAbbr` -> `string cityAbbr = ""`
   - `string source` -> `string source = ""`
   - `string tsj` -> `string tsj = ""`
   - `string importSrc` -> `string importSrc = ""`
   - Leave `clientNumber`, `series`, `code`, `amount`, `description` required (these are load-bearing).
   - Reorder so all required params come before defaulted ones (C# language requirement once you introduce defaults): final order would be `(clientNumber, series, code, amount, description, prefix = "", suffix = "", stateAbbr = "", cityAbbr = "", source = "", tsj = "", importSrc = "", replaceIndex = null, dryRun = false, idempotencyKey = null)`. Reordering is a breaking change for any positional callers, but MCP tool calls are JSON-named so no wire callers break; only the in-repo test fixtures need updating.

2. **Description rewrites** — change "often empty" wording to "Defaults to empty" so the JSON-schema enum-of-optional surfaces clearly to the LLM. Example: `"Prefix string. Defaults to empty — omit unless the row's natural key needs a prefix segment."`. Same pattern for the other six.

3. **Update test fixtures** in `SimulationStoreTests.cs`, `SimulationStoreConcurrencyTests.cs`, and `DetailWriteRoundTripTests.cs` — the `new DetailRow("X", "", "1", "", "", "", "", "", "", 1.0, "")` constructions are unaffected (DetailRow record is internal and unchanged), but any test that calls `LacerteDetailWrite` positionally with empty strings should be simplified to demonstrate the new minimal-arg path. Add one new test `DetailWrite_WithDefaults_OmitsAllOptionalStrings` that calls the tool with only the 5 required args and verifies the persisted row has empty strings for the rest — this both proves the fix and documents the new contract.

4. **README tool table** — update the `lacerte_detail_write` row to list the new required-vs-defaulted split, and add a one-line W-2 quick-example showing the 5-arg invocation. This surfaces the new affordance to the human operator who reads the README before wiring up Cursor/Claude Desktop.

5. **ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md** — add a bullet under §lacerte_detail_write noting "Optional row-key segments (prefix, suffix, stateAbbr, cityAbbr, source, tsj, importSrc) default to empty string; only series, code, clientNumber, amount, description are required."

6. **DECISIONS.md** — log a dated entry: "2026-05-30 — DetailWrite optional row-key params default to empty string to align with FieldWriteTools' nullable-default pattern and cut W-2 happy-path arg count from 12 to 5; reduces LLM token cost on the hottest write path and removes 7 typo surfaces per call."

The finding's 'positional misordering' framing is slightly inaccurate (MCP is JSON object, not positional), so do not lead with that justification in the commit message — frame the change as 'cross-tool consistency with FieldWrite + W-2 happy-path token reduction' instead.

title: Mojibake (Â§, â€") in FieldWriteBulkTools [Description] strings ships to every MCP client's tool catalog
userImpact: Every MCP client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, generic) that calls tools/list sees garbled byte sequences ('Â§2', 'â€" string, number, or boolean', 'idempotency â€" matches') in the lacerte_field_write_bulk tool description and several of its parameter descriptions. The LLM has trained on this exact mojibake pattern as 'corrupted text' and will downweight the tool, ask the operator to disambiguate, or skip it for the single-write tool — directly undermining the highest-priority workflow the bulk tool was added to enable (P15-008, REQUIREMENTS §1.2 mailing-address sweeps).
description: FieldWriteBulkTools.cs contains UTF-8 byte sequences for '§' and '—' that were decoded as Windows-1252 then re-saved as UTF-8 — the classic mojibake double-encoding. Confirmed with grep: line 17 has 'REQUIREMENTS Â§1.2', line 29 has 'for every row â€" NOT past it', line 66 (the BulkWriteEntry.Value [Description] which ships in the JSON schema sent to every MCP client), line 77 (the main [McpServerTool] description with two mojibake instances), lines 79/81/82 (parameter descriptions including '§2'/'Optional —'). These strings are NOT in C# comments — they are in `[Description(...)]` attributes which the MCP SDK serializes verbatim into the tools/list JSON-RPC response. Every other tool file in the project uses clean UTF-8 ('§', '—') so this one file is uniquely broken. Compare with FieldWriteTools.cs:41 or DetailsTools.cs:65 (same author intent, clean encoding). The file itself is genuine UTF-8 — the issue is upstream byte rot that survived a paste from a Windows-1252-defaulted editor.

Add a unit test in McpDiscoveryRoundtripTests.cs (the existing roundtrip harness) that fetches the lacerte_field_write_bulk tool descriptor, asserts the description string contains '§' AND does NOT contain any 'Â' / 'â€' bytes — this pins the regression so the next bad paste fails CI.
