Prompts are the LLM's main 'how do I drive this thing?' surface; an undocumented prompt is invisible to the operator until they happen to call `prompts/list` in their MCP host (Claude Desktop does not surface this UI by default).

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly: WorkflowPrompts.cs registers 4 `[McpServerPrompt(Name=...)]` methods at lines 36, 120, 177, 240 (lacerte_client_intake, lacerte_review_ef_status, lacerte_bulk_field_update, lacerte_csv_intake). README line 158 explicitly says 'Three first-class MCP prompts' and the table at 162-164 lists only the first three. The fourth prompt (`lacerte_csv_intake`) is the one most directly tied to a real tax-pro pain point — bulk client onboarding from a Tax Organizer export (REQUIREMENTS §1.3). Prior audits: round-1 finding (audit-findings.json:311 and :729) ADDED the Prompts section with 3 prompts; round-2 (G_prompts cluster at :901/:1171) tested prompts end-to-end but did not enumerate or count-check the README table. The CSV prompt clearly landed in a later P15 task without README sync — this is genuinely new drift, not a duplicate. Operator impact is real: Claude Desktop does not expose `prompts/list` in its UI, so the README's prompts table IS the discovery surface for a tax pro evaluating the server. An invisible bulk-intake prompt forces the operator to either chain `lacerte_client_intake` per row (slow, no idempotency batch key) or re-derive the workflow by hand. The suggested CI guard (assert README row count == discovered prompt count in McpDiscoveryRoundtripTests) is a small concrete addition that prevents this exact drift class from recurring.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Two-part fix. (1) README sync: change line 158 from 'Three first-class MCP prompts' to 'Four first-class MCP prompts' and append one table row after line 164: `| `lacerte_csv_intake` | Bulk-onboard clients from a CSV / Tax-Organizer export — operator declares column→field mapping once, prompt walks per-row create + seed with per-row idempotency keys and stop-on-first-error. Maps to REQUIREMENTS §1.3. | `sourceLabel?: string`, `rowCount: int = 0` |`. (2) Drift guard: add a test to `src/LacertMCP.Tests/Integration/McpDiscoveryRoundtripTests.cs` that reflects over `WorkflowPrompts` for `[McpServerPrompt]` methods, parses the README `## Prompts` table rows, and asserts (a) every registered prompt Name appears as a row, and (b) the count word in the sentence preceding the table matches (`Three`/`Four`/`Five`). This makes the next-prompt-without-README-sync fail CI rather than ship invisibly. Optionally add the prompt to `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md` if the other prompts are listed there.

title: README never tells the operator that `lacerte-mcp tools` is the canonical pre-install discovery + sanity-check verb
userImpact: Before pasting LacertMCP into Claude Desktop / Cursor, the operator wants to verify (a) the binary they downloaded actually registers the tools they expect, and (b) what arguments each tool wants. `lacerte-mcp tools --name lacerte_field_write` was built EXPRESSLY for this (ToolsCommand.cs lines 124-153 — full per-tool surface dump), and `--filter '^lacerte_ef_'` exists for grouping. But the README Tools section never mentions either flag, and the CLI section describes `tools` only as a flat dump. Operators end up reading the source to find tool signatures, or call the wrong tool with wrong args and grep the JSON-RPC log.
description: ToolsCommand.cs implements four discovery modes (table, `--json`, `--filter <regex>`, `--name <exact>`, `--names-only`). The `--name` mode is the moral equivalent of an MCP `tools/describe` endpoint — it prints one tool's full parameter list with descriptions, declaring type, optionality. The README's Tools section (line 122) shows the static table only and never tells the operator that they can introspect any tool's full surface offline. The CLI section (line 256) lists only `[--json]` and skips `--filter`, `--name`, and `--names-only`. The `lacerte_field_access_map` MCP tool fills the per-tool-schema gap for FIELDS but there is no MCP equivalent for 'describe an MCP tool' (e.g. `lacerte_describe_tool('lacerte_field_write')`) — `lacerte-mcp tools --name` is the only way and it is invisible.
recommendation: (1) In the README Tools section, add a one-paragraph 'Discovering tools at runtime' note pointing at `lacerte-mcp tools --name lacerte_field_write` (per-tool full surface), `lacerte-mcp tools --filter '^lacerte_ef_'` (regex group), and `--names-only` (pipe-friendly). Show a 3-line example output. (2) In the `### `lacerte-mcp tools`` CLI subsection (line 256), document all four flags, not just `--json`. (3) Consider adding a thin MCP-side `lacerte_describe_tool(name: string)` tool that wraps the same `ToolsCommand.DiscoverTools()` helper so the LLM can self-describe at the tool-use loop boundary without shelling out — the function is already public + reflection-only + cross-platform.
rationale: Round-2 covered the existence of P15-066 (`--filter`/`--name`) as a code addition but no audit round flagged the README/CLI-doc surface for these flags. The whole reason the operator runs `lacerte-mcp tools` is discoverability; if the README doesn't surface the discovery flags, the most useful affordance dies in the source comments.

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly: (1) README C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/README.md line 256 signature `lacerte-mcp tools [--json]` is the *only* shape shown and the body text mentions only `--json`. Grep for `--filter|--name|--names-only` across README returns zero matches. (2) ToolsCommand.cs lines 49-69 confirms all three flags exist, plus the deep `--name` deep-print branch at lines 124-153 that prints one tool's full per-parameter surface with descriptions — exactly the affordance an operator needs when wiring an MCP client and choosing tool args. (3) Tools section line 122-156 also gives no hint that runtime offline discovery exists. (4) Cross-checked prior audit work: P15-066 (audit-findings-r2.json line 1582-1609) added the flags as a code change; its `Do:` block only covers ToolsCommand.cs + tests. P14-045 documented per-CLI-subcommand flags but pre-dates P15-066. P14-046 only mandated `--json`. P14-047 is unrelated (Troubleshooting). So the README-surface gap is genuinely new and unaddressed. (5) User impact is real: a tax-pro operator pasting LacertMCP into Claude Desktop / Cursor today, who wants to verify their downloaded binary registers the tools they expect (or check a tool's exact parameter shape before composing a config), has no way to know `--name`/`--filter`/`--names-only` exist short of reading ToolsCommand.cs. Single-line awareness fix delivers most of the value. (6) The "add a thin MCP-side lacerte_describe_tool" sub-recommendation is bikeshedding — MCP clients already get full tool/parameter schemas via the standard `tools/list` JSON-RPC handshake on connect, so adding a wrapper tool is redundant. Drop that part; keep README docs + CLI subsection updates.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Two README edits, no code change required. (1) In the `### `lacerte-mcp tools`` CLI subsection at C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/README.md line 256, update the signature to `lacerte-mcp tools [--json] [--filter <regex>] [--name <exact>] [--names-only]` and replace the current `--json` bullet with a four-bullet list documenting each flag: `--json` (machine output), `--filter <regex>` (case-insensitive regex on tool name, e.g. `--filter '^lacerte_ef_'` for e-file tools, exit 2 on invalid regex), `--name <exact>` (deep-print one tool's full parameter surface incl. parameter descriptions, exit 1 on no match — recommend this when composing MCP client configs), `--names-only` (one tool name per line for pipelines/CI). (2) In the `## Tools` section near line 122, append a one-paragraph "Discovering tools at runtime" note pointing operators at `lacerte-mcp tools --name <toolName>` for the canonical per-tool signature dump (the README's static table can drift behind the code; `--name` always reflects the live assembly). Show a 3-line sample output of `lacerte-mcp tools --name lacerte_field_write` so the reader sees the per-parameter type + description format. Skip the "add an MCP-side `lacerte_describe_tool` wrapper" sub-recommendation from the original finding — MCP's standard `tools/list` handshake already delivers per-tool parameter schemas to Claude Desktop/Cursor on connect, so a wrapper tool is redundant; the gap is purely README discoverability for the CLI surface.

title: No way for the LLM (or operator) to enumerate valid (taxYear, module, dataPath) combos without trial-and-error — `lacerte_list_datapaths` returns only what's on disk and never explains the empty result
userImpact: An operator on a Windows box runs the MCP and the LLM calls `lacerte_list_datapaths` — gets back `{ root: 'C:\Lacerte', rootExists: false, count: 0, datapaths: [] }` because their Lacerte install is at `D:\Apps\Lacerte`. The response is technically true but completely opaque to the LLM, which now has no idea what to suggest. The remediation pattern in the rest of the codebase (e.g. README troubleshooting line 311) names the env var (`LACERTE_DATA_ROOT`) — but `lacerte_list_datapaths` does NOT include this remediation in the empty-result response. The operator is left wondering 'is Lacerte not installed?' / 'is the env var wrong?' / 'is the MCP broken?'
description: Three sub-issues compound: (a) the response shape includes `rootExists` but never says 'set LACERTE_DATA_ROOT to the actual install root if it lives elsewhere'. (b) There is no example-matrix in the README or in any prompt showing common combos (`C:\Lacerte\24Tax\IData` for individual TY24, `C:\Lacerte\23Tax\CData` for corporate TY23, etc.) — the README ONLY shows `C:\Lacerte\24data` (different shape: no `Tax` folder!), which contradicts the actual scanner pattern `{YY}Tax\{Module}Data` at SessionTools.cs:31-36. (c) There is no MCP-side tool that says 'I see Lacerte installed at X; here are the years/modules I found' as a single guided step — operators must chain `lacerte_list_datapaths` + then `lacerte_set_context` and guess the right tuple. The README env table line 91 even says `LACERTE_DATA_PATH=C:\Lacerte\24data` (lowercase `data`, no `Tax`) which is an entirely different shape than what `lacerte_list_datapaths` produces.
recommendation: (1) Expand the empty-result branch of `LacerteListDatapaths` to include a `hint` field naming the env var and the expected folder shape: `hint: "No {YY}Tax\{Module}Data subfolders found under \"" + root + "\". If Lacerte is installed elsewhere, set LACERTE_DATA_ROOT to that path and restart the MCP. Expected layout example: C:\Lacerte\24Tax\IData (Individual TY24), 23Tax\CData (Corporate TY23)"`. (2) Fix the README example `C:\Lacerte\24data` on line 91 to match the actual scanner pattern `C:\Lacerte\24Tax\IData` (or be explicit that `LACERTE_DATA_PATH` is the LEAF directory while `LACERTE_DATA_ROOT` is the ROOT — they have different shapes). (3) Add a small example-matrix section to README showing 3-4 canonical `(env var, value)` rows so an operator copy-pasting the Claude Desktop config has a concrete starting point. The README install snippet at line 60 already says `C:\Lacerte\24data` — three different surfaces tell three different stories about the on-disk layout.
rationale: Round-1 P14-016 covered the existence of LACERTE_DATA_ROOT and round-2 P15-002 covered env-table sync — neither flagged that the README's example path uses a different folder convention (`24data`) than the scanner's expected convention (`24Tax\IData`). Empty discovery results without hints are the second-most-common 'is the MCP broken?' moment after auth expiry; both deserve guided remediation in the response itself.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified all three sub-claims by reading SessionTools.cs:141-156, README.md (lines 50-101, 263-318), ConnectionStringBuilder.cs, SeedData.cs, PathValidation.cs, and SyntheticStatusCodes.cs, then cross-checking audit-findings.json (P14-016) and audit-findings-r2.json (P15-002, P15-004, P15-005).

(a) CONFIRMED — SessionTools.LacerteListDatapaths returns exactly `{ root, rootExists, count, datapaths }`. There is no `hint` field, no remediation string, and no mention of `LACERTE_DATA_ROOT`. When count=0 the LLM has nothing to suggest; the operator gets opaque silence. Round-1's P14-016 added the env var to the README env table; round-2's P15-002 added it to ARCHITECTURE.md; NEITHER touched the empty-result response shape. This is a genuine discoverability-tools gap not previously surfaced.

(b) CONFIRMED and STRONGER THAN THE FINDING CLAIMS — the codebase itself ships TWO different on-disk layout conventions:
- Scanner-side (SessionTools.cs:30-36, SeedData.cs:29-32, SessionContext.cs:11, SimulationStore.cs:13-21, PathValidation.cs:111, SessionTools.cs:70 description, SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:175): `C:\Lacerte\{YY}Tax\{Module}Data` (e.g. `24Tax\IData`).
- ODBC/test-side (ConnectionStringBuilder.cs:19,29 XML docs and every Bridge test — LacerteAccessClientTests/ReaderTests/SessionManagerBridgeWireupTests/BridgeInputValidationTests): `C:\Lacerte\YYdata\` (e.g. `24data`).
ConnectionStringBuilder.cs:19 literally says "the standard install layout (C:\Lacerte\YYdata\) mixes multiple modules in one directory" — directly contradicting the scanner's `{YY}Tax\{Module}Data` pattern at SessionTools.cs:30-36. README adds a THIRD wrinkle: line 59 + 91 use `24data` (lowercase d), line 309 troubleshooting uses `24Data` (uppercase D), neither matches the scanner. So three surfaces tell three different stories AND the code itself ships both conventions side-by-side, which strongly suggests both layouts exist in real Lacerte installs (per-module-leaf vs shared) and the doc must explain which one each tool expects, not just pick one. Not covered by P14-016 (env table only), P14-017 (doctor exit code), P15-002 (env table sync), P15-004 (DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR wiring), or P15-005 (APP_ID).

(c) Partial — there is no guided "I see Lacerte at X; here are the years/modules I found" single tool. The user must chain list_datapaths → set_context. This is a real ergonomic gap, but the simpler fix (hint field in empty result) addresses the most common failure case without inventing a new tool surface.

This meaningfully improves both LLM and operator experience: the empty-result moment is one of the first interactions a fresh operator hits, and right now it dead-ends silently. The README inconsistency is the kind that erodes trust the moment an operator notices it — and it WILL be noticed because the install snippet (line 59) and the discovery output use different shapes.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Three-part fix, all sim-friendly and high-leverage. Do them in this priority order:

(1) HIGHEST-VALUE — add a `hint` field to `LacerteListDatapaths` (SessionTools.cs:143-156) that fires in BOTH the missing-root and zero-results cases. Two distinct strings so the LLM can branch its suggestion:

  - If `!Directory.Exists(root)`: `hint = "Discovery root '" + root + "' does not exist. If Lacerte is installed elsewhere, set the LACERTE_DATA_ROOT env var to that path and restart the MCP. Expected layout: {root}\\{YY}Tax\\{Module}Data (e.g. C:\\Lacerte\\24Tax\\IData for Individual TY24, 23Tax\\CData for Corporate TY23). Modules: I/C/P/S/F/R/T/N/B."`
  - If root exists but `count == 0`: `hint = "Root '" + root + "' exists but contains no {YY}Tax\\{Module}Data subfolders. Either Lacerte is installed at a different root (set LACERTE_DATA_ROOT and restart), or this box uses the alternate shared layout C:\\Lacerte\\{YY}data\\ (in that case pass the leaf to lacerte_set_context directly — the scanner only finds the per-module shape)."`
  - If `count > 0`: omit the `hint` field entirely (don't pollute the happy path).

Add a single SessionToolsTests case asserting the hint string contains the literal substrings "LACERTE_DATA_ROOT" and "{YY}Tax\\{Module}Data" in both empty branches. Pure C# + sim test, no Windows needed.

(2) SECOND-MOST-VALUABLE — resolve the README's three-way layout-shape contradiction by NAMING both shapes explicitly rather than picking one. The codebase ships both because real Lacerte installs ship both (the ODBC tests use `24data`, the scanner expects `24Tax\IData`). Edit README.md as follows:

  - Line 59 (install snippet): change `"LACERTE_DATA_PATH": "C:\\Lacerte\\24data"` to `"LACERTE_DATA_PATH": "C:\\Lacerte\\24Tax\\IData"` and add a one-line comment above the env block: `// LACERTE_DATA_PATH is the LEAF data directory passed to set_context — typically C:\\Lacerte\\{YY}Tax\\{Module}Data (per-module shape) on modern installs, or C:\\Lacerte\\{YY}data (shared-module shape) on legacy installs. LACERTE_DATA_ROOT is the ROOT scanned by lacerte_list_datapaths.`
  - Line 91 (env table `LACERTE_DATA_PATH` row): change Purpose column to `Default datapath leaf (per-module e.g. C:\\Lacerte\\24Tax\\IData, or shared-module e.g. C:\\Lacerte\\24data). lacerte_list_datapaths only enumerates the per-module shape.`
  - Line 98 (env table `LACERTE_DATA_ROOT` row): add to Purpose `(scans for {YY}Tax\\{Module}Data subfolders only — does not enumerate the shared-module C:\\Lacerte\\{YY}data shape).`
  - Line 309 (troubleshooting): the current text already says `24Data` (uppercase D) — change to `C:\\Lacerte\\24Tax\\IData (or the shared-module C:\\Lacerte\\24data if your install uses that layout)` so the symptom example matches the actual scanner pattern.

(3) THIRD — add a 4-row example-matrix sub-bullet under the README env-vars section showing canonical `(env var, value)` pairs an operator can copy-paste:
  ```
  | Scenario | LACERTE_DATA_ROOT | LACERTE_DATA_PATH |
  |---|---|---|
  | Default install, TY24 Individual | (unset, uses C:\Lacerte) | C:\Lacerte\24Tax\IData |
  | Non-default root, TY24 Corporate | D:\Apps\Lacerte | D:\Apps\Lacerte\24Tax\CData |
  | Shared-module layout, TY24 Individual | (unset; list_datapaths returns 0) | C:\Lacerte\24data |
  | Network-mounted, TY23 Partnership | \\\\fileserver\\Lacerte | \\\\fileserver\\Lacerte\\23Tax\\PData |
  ```

DEFER the "single guided lacerte_discover_install" tool — it duplicates surface and a well-hinted lacerte_list_datapaths is sufficient. The bulk of the user impact is solved by (1) alone; (2) and (3) clean up the trust-eroding cross-doc contradictions that round-1/round-2 left in place. All three edits are pure docs + a single SessionTools.cs branch + a single unit test — no live Lacerte/Windows dependency.

title: `lacerte_reload_schema` and `lacerte_field_write_bulk` exist as registered tools but are entirely absent from the README Tools table
userImpact: An operator following the README to plan an MCP integration sees 21 tools listed (or fewer — count is implicit) but the actual server registers AT LEAST 23: every README-listed tool PLUS `lacerte_reload_schema` (SchemaReloadTools.cs) and `lacerte_field_write_bulk` (FieldWriteBulkTools.cs). `lacerte_field_write_bulk` is the canonical answer to 'I need to update mailing addresses on 300 clients' (per its own xmldoc) — but a tax pro reading the README would never discover it and would write a `lacerte_field_write` loop in their LLM prompt, hitting 300x the round-trips. `lacerte_reload_schema` is the OTHER half of the FieldAccessDumper workflow (per its own docs) but is invisible to operators, who would restart the server instead and invalidate their 24h Intuit auth ticket — a 5-minute consent-dialog ceremony to avoid.
description: Grep of `[McpServerTool]` decorations across `src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/` returns at least 23 tools. README Tools tables (lines 122-156) list 21. Missing: `lacerte_reload_schema` (Phase 8/13 follow-up — drops the schema cache so a fresh shard takes effect without restart) and `lacerte_field_write_bulk` (P15-008 — fans out N writes through one MCP call with per-row idempotency and error aggregation). Both are operator-critical; both have full xmldoc explaining why they exist; both are runtime-discoverable via `tools/list` but invisible to anyone reading the README to PLAN an integration. The McpDiscoveryRoundtripTests.cs file exists but only asserts the tools register — it does not cross-check the README table for completeness.
recommendation: Add two rows to the README Tools table — after row `lacerte_return_codes` add: `| `lacerte_field_write_bulk` | Single tool call that fans out N field writes through the WriteField chokepoint; per-row idempotency keys, per-row error aggregation, stop-on-first-error optional. Use for mailing-address sweeps, EF flag flips, preparer reassignments. | 8 |` and `| `lacerte_reload_schema` | Drop the in-process FieldAccessMap caches so a freshly written shard (e.g. from LacertMCP.FieldAccessDumper.exe) takes effect without restarting the server (which would invalidate the 24h Intuit auth ticket and force a re-register). | 13 |`. Strengthen `McpDiscoveryRoundtripTests` with an assertion that every runtime-registered tool name appears at least once in `README.md`, failing the build on the next undocumented-tool drift (same pattern as the prompts table check recommended above).
rationale: Round-2 P15-001 fixed README test counts but did not enumerate the tool surface; round-1 covered tool registration but not README-vs-runtime parity. The two missing tools are exactly the kind of mid-life-cycle additions (Phase 8/13/15) that drift past doc updates. The 'auth ticket invalidation by accidental restart' angle on `lacerte_reload_schema` is a real, high-friction operator pain (5-minute re-consent dance) — surfacing this tool in the README would directly reduce that friction.

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly. Grep of `[McpServerTool]` under src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/ returns 23 registered tools, including `LacerteFieldWriteBulk` (FieldWriteBulkTools.cs:76) and `LacerteReloadSchema` (SchemaReloadTools.cs:38). README.md Tools tables (lines 122-156) list 21 tools split across Phase-5 reads and Phase-6-8 writes/metadata — neither table row mentions `lacerte_field_write_bulk` or `lacerte_reload_schema`. Grep across the full README for either name returns zero hits (not in Tools, not in Prompts, not in Troubleshooting, not in Errors). Both tools shipped in Phase 15 with substantial xmldoc explaining why they exist: FieldWriteBulkTools is the canonical answer to the 300-client mailing-address sweep (the operator scenario REQUIREMENTS §1.2 calls out and the `lacerte_bulk_field_update` prompt currently loops `lacerte_field_write` to work around) and SchemaReloadTools is explicitly the cure for "I ran the dumper, do I need to restart and re-consent?" — the 5-minute Intuit-24h-ticket-invalidation ceremony. The Round-2 verdicts for P15-008 and P15-044 spec'd the tools but the README Tools-table rows were never landed. No prior finding flags the README-vs-runtime parity gap; no test (including McpDiscoveryRoundtripTests) cross-checks the README. This is a genuine discoverability bug: an operator who plans an integration off the README will (a) never find the bulk tool and pay N round-trips for the firm-wide write they came to do, and (b) never find the reload tool and trip the auth-re-consent path. Both are concrete, real moments of friction this fix would eliminate. Not bikeshedding — this is the README failing at its primary job (the planning surface for the operator).
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Two README edits + one test, all sim-runnable off-Windows:

1. **README.md Write / Create / Metadata table (line 145-154)** — append two rows after `lacerte_return_codes`:
   - `| \`lacerte_field_write_bulk\` | Single tool call that fans out N field writes through the same WriteField chokepoint as lacerte_field_write. Per-row idempotency keys (suffix = clientNumber), per-row error aggregation in { succeeded, failed, skipped }, stop-on-first-error default with continueOnError opt-in. Use for mailing-address sweeps, EF flag flips, preparer reassignments — REQUIREMENTS §1.2's primary bulk-write flow. | 15 |`
   - `| \`lacerte_reload_schema\` | Drop the in-process FieldAccessMap caches so freshly written shards (e.g. from LacertMCP.FieldAccessDumper.exe) take effect without restarting the server. Restarting would invalidate the Intuit 24h auth ticket and force the 5-minute re-consent ceremony — call this tool instead. Returns { modulesReloaded, overlaysReloaded }. | 15 |`

2. **README.md Troubleshooting section** — add a bullet under the dumper workflow: \"If the FieldAccessDumper produced fresh shards but writes still return 9012 UnknownFieldAccess, call the `lacerte_reload_schema` MCP tool — do NOT restart the server, that invalidates your 24h auth ticket.\" (This was promised in P15-044's refinedRecommendation but never landed.)

3. **McpDiscoveryRoundtripTests.cs** — add a `[Fact] EveryRegisteredToolIsDocumentedInReadme()` that reads README.md once, enumerates the runtime tool registry the same way the existing roundtrip test does, and asserts every tool name appears at least once in the README text. Fails the build on the next undocumented-tool drift — same pattern recommended for the prompts table. Keep the assertion message specific (\"Tool '{name}' is registered at runtime but is missing from README.md — add a row to the Tools table at line ~122\") so future contributors get a direct fix path.

3. **WorkflowPrompts.cs `BulkFieldUpdate`** — while editing, also retarget the prompt's primary recommendation to `lacerte_field_write_bulk` and demote the per-row `lacerte_field_write` loop to a fallback note (this closes the loop on P15-008 — the prompt currently still walks the LLM through the slow path it was built to replace).

title: README + CLI claim doctor runs 7 probes; actual is ~13 — operator will tick wrong number of green/red lines
userImpact: Operator reads "Exit 0 means all 7 probes are green" (README:112), runs `lacerte-mcp doctor`, sees ~13 probe rows printed. They'll either think the CLI is broken or that they're reading the wrong README. The 7-probe list in README.md:273 is also a strict subset — it omits App.config shim, COM ProgID, Operating mode, LACERTE_DATA_ROOT, FieldAccessMap shards, and the Build version row, so an operator reading the README to know what "all green" looks like is missing 6 lines.
description: README.md:112 says "Exit 0 means all 7 probes are green (Windows version, x64 process, .NET 4.8, ODBC DSN, SDK install dir, env, AppID)." README.md:226 says "7-probe setup verification". README.md:273 says "Seven-probe setup verification". REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:130 says "all 7 probes green". Actual DoctorCommand.cs builds a list with: Build version, Windows version, x64, App.config shim, .NET 4.8, ODBC DSN, Lacerte SDK install, Lacerte COM ProgID, Operating mode, LACERTE_DATA_PATH env+dir, LACERTE_DATA_ROOT env+dir, FieldAccessMap shards, AppID. That's 13 (and ProbeDataPathEnv returns multiple ProbeResults per env var, so the visible row count is even higher).
recommendation: Replace the hard-coded "7" with a brief enumeration that matches the current probe set, or drop the count and link to the source-of-truth list in DoctorCommand.cs's XML doc (lines 29-34 already enumerate). REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:130 should say "all probes green". README.md:226 table row: "Setup verification; exit 0/1/2 contract." — drop the count. The XML doc on DoctorCommand has the most current list — make README cite that.
rationale: Counted probe-emission sites in DoctorCommand.cs:228-343 (Build, Windows, x64, App.config, .NET 4.8, ODBC, SDK install, COM ProgID, Operating mode, DATA_PATH env, DATA_ROOT env, shards, AppID = 13 distinct probe categories). Hard-coded 7 in 4 doc locations is stale.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all four cited doc sites: README.md:112 ("all 7 probes are green (Windows version, x64 process, .NET 4.8, ODBC DSN, SDK install dir, env, AppID)"), README.md:226 ("7-probe setup verification"), README.md:273 ("Seven-probe setup verification: Windows version, x64 process, .NET 4.8, ODBC DSN, SDK install dir, env vars (LACERTE_DATA_PATH), persisted AppID"), and REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:130 ("all 7 probes green"). Counted DoctorCommand.RunAllProbes (src/LacertMCP.Cli/Commands/DoctorCommand.cs:224-343): 13 distinct probe categories — Build version, Windows version, x64, App.config shim, .NET 4.8, ODBC DSN, Lacerte SDK install, Lacerte COM ProgID, Operating mode, LACERTE_DATA_PATH env (+ directory when set), LACERTE_DATA_ROOT env (+ directory when set), FieldAccessMap shards, AppID GUID. The XML doc on DoctorCommand (lines 28-34) already enumerates them all correctly — only the README + REGRESSION_CHECKLIST are stale. This is a PARTIAL-FIX follow-up to r2 task P15-031, whose refinedRecommendation explicitly said "update the DoctorCommand XML doc (lines 22-27) to list all 13 probes, AND update README quick-start which currently lists 7." The code/XML half landed; the README/checklist half did not. Not duplicated in r1 or r2 as a standalone open finding. User impact is real on the highest-friction first-touch surface (operator install verification) — an operator who reads README:112 then runs doctor and sees Build version / App.config shim / Lacerte COM ProgID / Operating mode / LACERTE_DATA_ROOT / FieldAccessMap shards (six rows the README enumeration omits) will reasonably second-guess whether the binary and docs match. Fix is a 3-minute markdown edit across 4 sites with no code/test risk.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Pure doc fix, no code/test changes. Four edits, all in-session:

(1) README.md:112 — Replace `Exit 0 means all 7 probes are green (Windows version, x64 process, .NET 4.8, ODBC DSN, SDK install dir, env, AppID).` with: `Exit 0 means every probe is green. The doctor surface covers OS/runtime (Windows, x64, .NET 4.8, App.config shim), install (ODBC DSN, Lacerte SDK install dir, Lacerte COM ProgID), config (operating mode, LACERTE_DATA_PATH, LACERTE_DATA_ROOT, FieldAccessMap shards), and identity (AppID GUID) — see DoctorCommand.cs XML doc for the canonical, always-current list.`

(2) README.md:226 — Change table row from `| `lacerte-mcp doctor` | 7-probe setup verification; exit 0/1/2 contract. |` to `| `lacerte-mcp doctor` | Multi-probe setup verification; exit 0/1/2 contract. |`. Drop the count entirely — it's a table TLDR; the detail section below carries the enumeration.

(3) README.md:271-273 — Rewrite the section header + first sentence. Current `### `lacerte-mcp doctor`` / `Seven-probe setup verification: Windows version, x64 process, .NET 4.8, ODBC DSN, SDK install dir, env vars (`LACERTE_DATA_PATH`), persisted AppID.   - Update the `[Description]` attribute (lines 178-181) to say "References lacerte_field_write_bulk" instead of "lacerte_field_write".
