title: limit=0 (and negative) silently returns the FULL set instead of zero rows
userImpact: An LLM that asks for `limit: 0` intending 'just give me the count/total' (or a UI that defensively passes 0 before incrementing) instead gets the FULL roster — up to int.MaxValue rows for ListClients. With a 5k-client firm that overshoots the MCP message-size limit and looks like an unrelated transport failure to the operator.
description: Pagination.Page uses `if (!limit.HasValue || limit.Value <= 0) { effectiveLimit = total - effectiveOffset; }`. That bucket conflates THREE caller intents — 'omitted/null' (unbounded), 'zero' (no rows), and 'negative' (probably a bug). All three resolve to 'send everything from offset to end'. The Description on every paginated tool says 'Default 100, clamped to Pagination.MaxLimit (1000)' which strongly implies an upper bound only — nothing hints that limit=0 is the unbounded sentinel. A reasonable LLM call pattern is `limit: total >= cap ? cap : remaining` and an off-by-one to `0` blows past the cap. Tools that pass `int limit = 100` (ClientsTools, TablesTools, DetailsTools) further hide that null is not even reachable — the only way to opt into the 'unbounded' branch from those tools is `0` or `-N`, which is exactly the wrong default for the surprising semantic.
recommendation: Make the semantics explicit and consistent: (a) treat `limit == 0` as 'return zero rows, but include `total` and `hasMore=true` so callers can use it as a cheap count probe' OR clamp `<=0` to `DefaultLimit` (100) and document it on the tool Descriptions. Either is fine; the current 'silently return everything' is the worst of the three. Add unit tests `Page_LimitZero_*` and `Page_NegativeLimit_*` to PaginationTests.cs (currently only covers negative OFFSET) to lock the chosen contract. Also update each tool's Description string to say what `limit: 0` actually does.
rationale: Round-1 P14-014 and round-2 P15-040 covered the pagination contract uniformity and SQL push-down but never specified `limit=0` / negative behavior. The PaginationTests file has 7 tests covering NoLimit, smaller-than-total, offset+limit, offset-beyond-end, negative-offset, clamping, and last-page — but no zero-or-negative limit test.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified all claims against source:

1. CONFIRMED — Pagination.cs:51-58 reads `if (!limit.HasValue || limit.Value <= 0) { effectiveLimit = total - effectiveOffset; }` — explicitly conflating null, zero, and negative into the unbounded branch. XML doc on lines 19-22 says "When `limit` is null OR non-positive the page is the full source" — so the behavior IS documented in source, but invisible at the tool layer.

2. CONFIRMED — All three paginated tools (ClientsTools.cs:26, TablesTools.cs:28, DetailsTools.cs:68) declare parameters as non-nullable `int limit = 100` with `[Description("Maximum rows to return. Default 100, clamped to Pagination.MaxLimit (1000).")]`. The Description strongly implies an upper-bound only — nothing hints that 0/negative means "unbounded." Because the parameter is non-nullable, the null branch is unreachable from the tool surface; the ONLY way to opt into "unbounded" from these tools is 0 or -N, which is the most surprising possible semantic for those values.

3. CONFIRMED — PaginationTests.cs has exactly 7 tests covering: NoLimitNoOffset, LimitSmallerThanTotal, LimitAndOffset, OffsetBeyondEnd, NegativeOffset (treated as zero), LimitLargerThanMax (clamped), LastPage. ZERO tests for limit==0 or negative limit. Contract is unspecified.

4. CONFIRMED NEW — Searched both audit files. Prior pagination findings: P14-014 (push-down O(n) perf), P14-036 (acceptance-criteria sync), P14-037 (DECISIONS entry), P15-009 (detail filter), P15-010 (ef_status filter), P15 retrofit (6 more tools). None specify or test limit=0/negative behavior.

5. User-moment is real but moderate: an LLM that uses `limit: total - already_fetched` and hits an off-by-one to 0 (a known LLM arithmetic failure mode), or one that defensively probes with `limit: 0` to get total before paging — both trigger a full-roster dump. With the F14/F15 plumbing also paginating EF status, details, forms, etc., the blast radius now spans more tools. ClientsTools still passes int.MaxValue to ListClients (per audit comment on lines 32-44), so for a 5k-client firm a limit=0 call materializes 5k CloneRow operations and ships them all over MCP — exceeding typical MCP transport size limits and presenting as an opaque transport failure to the operator.

Not bikeshedding: this is a "trap door" parameter value that produces the worst-case outcome silently. Fix is ~3 lines + 2 tests + Description edits — small, pure-sim, off-Windows actionable.

Meaningfully improves: yes — removes a sharp edge that turns a plausible LLM call pattern into a transport failure. The Description-string clarification alone is a real LLM-UX win (telling the LLM "limit=0 returns zero rows + total, useful as a cheap count probe" gives it a deliberate idiom for the "just count" intent instead of leaving the question open).

title: LacerteClientCreate accepts lowercase ClientID via IgnoreCase regex but doesn't uppercase before passing to the SDK — case ambiguity on the wire
userImpact: Operator passes `clientID: 'abc1'`; tool accepts it (regex is IgnoreCase), CreateClientArgs carries 'abc1' literal into the live SDK. Lacerte's ClientID convention is uppercase alphanumeric; depending on the SDK version the COM call may silently uppercase, may reject with InValidClientName (24), or may store mixed-case and break later folder lookups (since the on-disk file path uses the ClientID verbatim). The downstream surprise is hard to diagnose because client-side validation passed.
description: Regex on line 32-34 is `new Regex(@"^[A-Z0-9]+$", RegexOptions.Compiled | RegexOptions.IgnoreCase | RegexOptions.CultureInvariant)`. IgnoreCase means 'abc1' matches even though the regex literal reads 'A-Z only'. The tool then passes `clientID` verbatim into `CreateClientArgs(ClientID: clientID, ...)`. The XML doc on the Description string says `<= 8 chars, alphanumeric only` — it does not commit to uppercase. ClientID is ALSO the basis for the on-disk `{CLIENT}.{Mod}{YY}` filename per DetailsTools.cs:13, where Windows is case-insensitive at the filesystem layer but case-PRESERVING — so a lowercase ClientID lands in the file path verbatim. Two callers using 'abc1' and 'ABC1' would target the SAME file via two DIFFERENT ClientIDs through this tool with no warning.
recommendation: Either (a) drop the `RegexOptions.IgnoreCase` flag so lowercase is rejected at validation time with a clear 'must be uppercase' error, OR (b) keep the permissive accept but uppercase the ClientID with `clientID = clientID.ToUpperInvariant()` before the regex check and before constructing CreateClientArgs. Option (b) is operator-friendlier (no rejection on common LLM-formatted input); option (a) is correctness-first. Either way, add a unit test `Create_LowercaseClientID_NormalizedToUpper` or `..._Rejected`. Also update the Description to commit to whatever the chosen contract is.
rationale: Round-1 P14-032 noted 'Sim CreateClient bypasses Registration, TaxType-Module, and ClientID-regex gates' which was about whether sim ran the regex. Round-2 did not address the IgnoreCase / non-normalizing accept. Verified by direct read of CreateClientTools.cs lines 32-34 and 212-217 — no `ToUpperInvariant()` call exists between regex check and CreateClientArgs construction.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by direct file reads. The finding accurately describes the bug, but the most damaging consequence is different from (and stronger than) what the finding leads with — it's a sim/live divergence + late-bind error UX issue, not primarily a filesystem-collision issue.

CONFIRMED FACTS:
1. CreateClientTools.cs:32-34 — regex is `^[A-Z0-9]+$` with `RegexOptions.IgnoreCase`, so `"abc1"` passes the tool-layer gate. No `ToUpperInvariant()` exists between the regex check (line 93) and `CreateClientArgs(ClientID: clientID, ...)` (line 213). Verified by Grep — only three `ToUpperInvariant` calls in src/LacertMCP.Server exist, none in CreateClientTools.cs.

2. **Cross-layer asymmetry (worse than the finding states):** BridgeInputValidation.cs:36-38 declares `ClientNumberPattern = new Regex("^[A-Z0-9]{1,8}$", Compiled | CultureInvariant)` — NO IgnoreCase flag. The CreateClient bridge path (LacerteAccessClient.cs:221) calls `BridgeInputValidation.ValidateCreateClientArgs(...)` which calls `ValidateClientNumber(clientID, op)` (BridgeInputValidation.cs:594). So in LIVE mode a lowercase `clientID` that passed the tool-layer regex throws `InValidClientName` (24) at the bridge boundary — after the operator was told the input is valid. This is exactly the kind of "ugly/confusing output" the round-3 lens is hunting for.

3. **Sim mode silently succeeds.** SimulationStore.cs:267-269 mirrors the tool regex (also IgnoreCase) and SimulateCreateClient (line 491) stores `args.ClientID` verbatim into row Fields["ClientID"] at line 540 (case-preserved). So sim accepts lowercase happily, live rejects — a direct violation of CLAUDE.md's "Simulation and live must be observationally identical for the happy path." The two-mode invariant the project's OS file makes non-negotiable is broken on a documented common input.

4. **The finding's filesystem-collision angle is weaker than claimed.** The on-disk `{CLIENT}.{Mod}{YY}` filename uses `clientNumber` (the SDK-minted integer per SimulationStore.cs:531-543), not the operator-supplied `clientID`. SQL path queries also use `clientNumber`, not `clientID`. So the "two callers using 'abc1' and 'ABC1' would target the SAME file via DIFFERENT ClientIDs" claim is incorrect — they'd be assigned different clientNumbers. The real damage is the sim/live divergence + the tool-says-valid/bridge-says-invalid UX, both of which are independently sufficient to justify the fix.

5. **Subtle additional bug in sim:** SimulateCreateClient's dup check at SimulationStore.cs:522 is case-insensitive (`OrdinalIgnoreCase`), but the stored ClientID at line 540 is case-preserving. So a sim caller who first creates "abc1" then queries by ClientID "ABC1" will hit case-sensitive lookups elsewhere with confusing misses — first-write-wins case becomes load-bearing trivia.

NOT A DUPLICATE: Grep on both audit-findings.json and audit-findings-r2.json for ClientID + uppercase/lowercase/IgnoreCase/normaliz returns only (a) P14-029 about FieldAccessMapLoader's lowercase field-name bypass (different code path), (b) P14-032 about sim CreateClient bypassing gates (since fixed; orthogonal to case-normalization), (c) P15-020 about CreateClient bridge boundary validation (added the bridge-boundary check that is now in fact the bug's surfacing point — but never added IgnoreCase symmetry between tool/bridge or normalized clientID at any layer). No prior finding addresses the IgnoreCase flag or case normalization at the CreateClient layer.

MEANINGFUL IMPROVEMENT? Yes. The operator running on Windows in live mode would get an `InValidClientName` (24) AFTER their tool call was implicitly accepted — confusing late-binding error. The LLM hosting the operator's session has no way to predict this since the tool-layer regex appears to accept the input. Cross-mode divergence directly violates the project's foundational two-mode discipline rule. Fix is one line. Easy win, real UX impact.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
**Option (b) is the right choice — uppercase-normalize, don't reject** — and apply the same normalization in the sim path so the two modes truly agree.

**Concrete fix (CreateClientTools.cs):**

Insert after the null/length checks but BEFORE the regex IsMatch at line 93:
```csharp
// Normalize case so lowercase operator-formatted input (common from LLM-
// generated tool calls) doesn't slip past the IgnoreCase regex and then
// get late-rejected by the case-sensitive ClientNumberPattern at the bridge
// boundary (BridgeInputValidation.cs:36) — same normalization the sim
// store needs (SimulationStore.cs:540 stores ClientID verbatim today).
clientID = clientID.ToUpperInvariant();
```

This single line makes the IgnoreCase regex semantically honest (still permissive accept, but the value passed downstream matches the strict pattern at every other layer) and closes the sim/live divergence. The downstream `CreateClientArgs(ClientID: clientID, ...)` at line 213 picks up the normalized value automatically.

**Mirror in SimulationStore.SimulateCreateClient (SimulationStore.cs:491):** add the same `args = args with { ClientID = args.ClientID?.ToUpperInvariant() ?? "" };` at the top of the method (it's a record, so `with` works) — OR drop `RegexOptions.IgnoreCase` from `_rxClientId` (line 269) so sim rejects lowercase the same way the bridge would. The former preserves the "tool already normalized so sim doesn't have to" property but defends against direct sim callers that skip the tool layer (which exist — there are integration tests that call SimulateCreateClient directly). The latter is correctness-first. Pick the `with` form to stay consistent with the tool-layer permissive-accept.

**Tests to add** in CreateClientToolsTests.cs:
1. `Create_LowercaseClientID_NormalizedToUpper_Succeeds` — call with `clientID: "abc1"`, assert the returned `clientID` field in the response equals `"ABC1"`, assert the stored DATA1 row Fields["ClientID"] equals `"ABC1"`.
2. `Create_MixedCaseClientID_NormalizedToUpper_Succeeds` — call with `"AbC1"`, assert normalized.
3. `Create_LowercaseClientID_DupCheckUsesNormalizedForm` — create `"abc1"` then attempt `"ABC1"`, assert `DuplicateClient` (already case-insensitive; just covers that normalization didn't break it).
4. In SimulationStoreTests: `SimulateCreateClient_LowercaseClientID_NormalizedAndStored` — call SimulateCreateClient directly with lowercase, assert the stored Fields["ClientID"] is uppercase.

**Doc updates:**
- CreateClientTools.cs:51 `[Description("Operator-chosen ClientID. <= 8 chars, alphanumeric only.")]` — append `" Lowercase is accepted and normalized to uppercase before storage."` so the LLM sees the contract.
- ARCHITECTURE.md or wherever the two-mode discipline is documented: add a one-line note that ClientID normalization happens at the tool layer + sim layer, mirroring the bridge's strict case-sensitive boundary.

**Optional follow-up (not required for this task):** Audit other validation regexes in the project for IgnoreCase + downstream case-sensitive consumers. State abbreviations are already symmetric (both `^[A-Z]{2}$` strict in DetailsTools.cs:36 AND BridgeInputValidation.cs:42-44), so no fix needed there. Field names have a similar issue but were addressed in P14-029.

Skip the "Option (a) reject lowercase" path — operator-friendliness wins given how often LLMs lowercase identifiers in tool calls.

title: stateAbbrev filter on read tools silently returns 0 rows on lowercase / whitespace input instead of normalizing or warning
userImpact: Operator/LLM passes `stateAbbrev: 'ca'` or `'CA '` or `'California'` to LacerteTableRead or LacerteStateRead expecting a filter on California rows. The session does `string.Equals(r.StateAbbrev, stateAbbrev, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)` — so 'ca' matches 'CA' fine (lowercase OK), but 'CA ' (trailing space) and 'California' silently return 0 rows. The tool returns `{ count: 0, states: [] }` with no diagnostic. The operator sees 'no California data exists' when actually the data is fine and only the filter input was off.
description: DetailsTools.LacerteDetailWrite validates `stateAbbr` against `^[A-Z]{2}$` (DetailsTools.cs:35-37, 201-211) and produces a structured DetailWriteInvalid error with a clear reason if the input is malformed. The READ path on `TablesTools.LacerteTableRead` (line 27), `StatesTools.LacerteStateRead` (line 24), and `StatesTools.LacerteStateSubclientRead` (line 41) has no equivalent validation — input is passed through to `_session.ReadTable` and used in an OrdinalIgnoreCase equality with no trimming or format check. Cross-tool inconsistency: same parameter, validated on write, ignored on read. The empty-result is indistinguishable from a legitimate 'no rows match' which is the most common case.
recommendation: In LacerteSessionManager.ReadTableCore, after the `if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(stateAbbrev))` guard, run `var trimmed = stateAbbrev.Trim();` — if the trimmed value is non-empty and not 2 ASCII letters, throw `LacerteSDKError(SyntheticStatusCodes.InvalidDataPath, { reason: 'stateAbbrev must be a 2-letter US/territory postal code (e.g. CA, NY); got X.', value: stateAbbrev })`. Mirrors the write-side gate at DetailsTools.cs:201-211 exactly. Lifts the silent-empty-result footgun into a structured error the LLM can correct from.
rationale: Round-1 P14-016 covered prefix filter behavior on ListClients; round-2 P15-040 covered pagination on these tools. Neither round flagged the read/write asymmetry on stateAbbrev format validation — verified by grepping `_rxStateAbbr` (only in DetailsTools.cs) and checking ReadTableCore for any normalize/validate step.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by direct file read. All four code citations are accurate:

1. C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/TablesTools.cs:27 — `stateAbbrev` parameter passed straight through to `_session.ReadTable` with no validation/normalization.
2. C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/StatesTools.cs:24, 41 — same pattern on LacerteStateRead and LacerteStateSubclientRead.
3. C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Server/Session/LacerteSessionManager.cs:719-722 — `string.Equals(r.StateAbbrev, stateAbbrev, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)` with no `Trim()` and no shape check.
4. C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/DetailsTools.cs:35-37, 201-211 — the write path validates `stateAbbr` against `^[A-Z]{2}$` and throws `LacerteSDKError(SyntheticStatusCodes.DetailWriteInvalid, { field: 'stateAbbr', value, reason: 'StateAbbr must be empty OR a 2-letter uppercase postal code (e.g. CA, NY).' })`. There's even a test fixture at DetailsToolsTests.cs:132 asserting `'California'` is rejected on write.

Not a duplicate. P14-016 is about README env-vars (not prefix filtering — the finding's own rationale citation is slightly off there). P15-040 retrofits these same tools with pagination but only mentions stateAbbrev in passing as 'already filterable'; it does not address validation/normalization. Grepping for `stateAbbrev.*Trim|stateAbbrev.*normalize|stateAbbrev.*lowercase` across both audit JSONs returns no prior coverage.

The usability case is genuine though moderate. The case-sensitivity angle in the finding is partially overstated — lowercase `'ca'` DOES work because of `OrdinalIgnoreCase`. The real wins are (a) trailing-whitespace `'CA '` silently returns 0 rows, (b) full-name `'California'` silently returns 0 rows, and (c) the cross-tool inconsistency itself: tax-pro types `stateAbbr: 'California'` into a DetailWrite and gets a clear structured error; the same operator types `stateAbbrev: 'California'` into a TableRead/StateRead and gets `{ count: 0, states: [] }` which is indistinguishable from 'no California data for this client.' That's a real trust footgun for a workflow where 'how many California clients do I have?' is a typical question. Fix is ~5 lines, mirrors an existing validator exactly, fully sim-actionable. Not bikeshedding — it lifts a silent failure mode into a structured error the LLM can self-correct from in one turn.

title: `./scripts/release.ps1` produces zip at `dist/LacertMCP-v0.1.0/LacertMCP-v0.1.0.zip`, README claims `dist/LacertMCP-v0.1.0.zip`
userImpact: The operator runs `./scripts/release.ps1` as the README instructs, then looks in `dist/` for `LacertMCP-v0.1.0.zip`, sees only a `LacertMCP-v0.1.0/` folder, opens it, then has to walk in to find the zip. Small friction but it erodes 'I followed the docs and they were right' trust on first contact, and any scripted install (`unzip dist/LacertMCP-v0.1.0.zip`) will fail with file-not-found.
description: P15-075 reworked release.ps1 to nest the staging under `LacertMCP-v$Version/` for destructive-wipe safety: `$stageRoot = Join-Path $staging "LacertMCP-v$Version"` then `$zipPath = Join-Path $stageRoot "LacertMCP-v$Version.zip"` (release.ps1 L156-196). So the real artifact path is `dist/LacertMCP-v0.1.0/LacertMCP-v0.1.0.zip`. README.md L50 still reads `produce dist/LacertMCP-v0.1.0.zip` from before the P15-075 path change. The script's own success message at L208 even calls out `==> Release artifact: $zipPath` with the nested path, so the script is self-consistent — only the README has drifted.
recommendation: One-line README edit: change `dist/LacertMCP-v0.1.0.zip` to `dist/LacertMCP-v0.1.0/LacertMCP-v0.1.0.zip`, or add a note that the zip is staged alongside the unpacked tree. Optionally, also have release.ps1 emit a `dist/latest.zip` symlink/copy so unattended installers have a stable path.
rationale: This is a doc-vs-code drift introduced by P15-075 (round 2) that round-2's doc-consistency lens missed because it didn't run the script end-to-end and compare the output path against the prose.

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly: C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/README.md line 50 reads `produce dist/LacertMCP-v0.1.0.zip`, but C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/scripts/release.ps1 lines 156 and 196 build the artifact at `$stageRoot/LacertMCP-v$Version.zip` where `$stageRoot = Join-Path $staging \"LacertMCP-v$Version\"` — the real path is `dist/LacertMCP-v0.1.0/LacertMCP-v0.1.0.zip`. The script's own success print at line 208 (`Release artifact: $zipPath`) emits the correct nested path, confirming README is the only place that drifted. Not duplicated: round-1 audit-findings.json predates the script's existence; round-2 P15-075 (Todo.md line 816, marked complete) introduced the nested staging for wipe-safety but neither the task nor its refinedRecommendation flagged the now-stale README. Round-2 doc-consistency lens missed it because it didn't end-to-end-execute release.ps1 and diff the produced path against README prose. The fix is one-line and meaningfully improves the first-install moment — operators copy-paste from README, and any automation/LLM following `unzip dist/LacertMCP-v0.1.0.zip` hard-fails with file-not-found. Barely passes the meaningfullyImproves bar because the script's success message does volunteer the correct path, but README is canonical for unattended installs and trust-on-first-contact, so this is worth shipping.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Edit C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/README.md line 50 from `produce dist/LacertMCP-v0.1.0.zip` to `produce dist/LacertMCP-v0.1.0/LacertMCP-v0.1.0.zip (the zip is staged inside a per-version subdirectory so prior release artifacts aren't wiped — see scripts/release.ps1)`. Keep the parenthetical brief so the install snippet stays scannable; the cross-reference explains the otherwise-surprising nesting and pre-empts a "why is there a folder AND a zip?" support question. Skip the `dist/latest.zip` symlink suggestion from the original finding — symlinks need elevated rights on Windows by default and add a moving target that can drift from the versioned artifact; the operator's MCP config already pins a fully-qualified install path so a stable filename buys nothing here. Optional bonus: in scripts/release.ps1 line 209, append the exact `Expand-Archive -Path \"$zipPath\" -DestinationPath C:\\LacertMCP -Force` command to the success message so the operator can copy-paste without re-typing the nested path.

title: `lacerte-mcp status` on a fresh checkout says `Registered: no` but never tells the operator what to run next
userImpact: The first command an operator runs (`./scripts/smoke.ps1` → `lacerte-mcp status`) on a clean clone prints `Registered: no` with no remediation hint. Compare with `doctor` which (per README L41) explicitly says `run lacerte-mcp register`. The status command has the *exact same* information needed to know whether `register` or sim-mode env vars are the next step, but emits no guidance. Operator has to context-switch back to README to figure out what to do.
description: StatusCommand.Run prints a 7-line table ending with `Build` and exits 0. When `appId.HasValue` is false, the human-format output writes only `Registered : no`. The CLI has all the data needed to give an actionable next step — it knows `mode` (live vs simulation), it knows `platform` (Windows vs not), it knows `backend`. The user-facing message could be: '→ next: run `lacerte-mcp register` to mint an AppID and grant Intuit consent (live mode), or set `LACERTE_SIMULATION=1` to use the in-memory seed.' The JSON path (`--json`) is API-shaped and should not be touched, but the default human path is meant for an operator and should be self-curing.
recommendation: In StatusCommand.cs after the `Build` line, append a tiny `Next:` block when `!appId.HasValue`: on Windows print `Run \`lacerte-mcp register\` to set up live mode, or set LACERTE_SIMULATION=1 to use the seeded sim store.` On non-Windows print `Sim mode is the only option here — point your MCP client at LacertMCP.Server.exe with LACERTE_SIMULATION=1.` Two extra lines, zero schema impact, hugely closes the 'now what?' gap.
rationale: Round-2 P15-026 added the human-readable format to status but stopped at 'show the data.' It did not cross the line into 'guide the user to the next command' that `doctor` already does.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading StatusCommand.cs (lines 110-123) and DoctorCommand.cs (lines 779-800), plus prior round-2 task P15-026 (which only added the human-readable format but stopped at 'show the data'). The asymmetry is real: when no AppID is persisted, doctor's ProbeAppId emits a Fail with the precise remediation 'Run `lacerte-mcp register` to mint and store one.' (line 798) — status, for the same state, prints only 'Registered : no' (line 112) and stops. The smoke script (scripts/smoke.ps1 line 55) calls `status` on every fresh build, so this is the literal first line of CLI output an operator sees on a clean clone. The CLI has every input needed (`mode`, `platform`, `appId.HasValue`) to print a context-appropriate next step at zero cost. The R2 P15-026 verdict explicitly scoped itself to JSON-vs-human polarity and did not address the guidance gap. Fix is tiny (3-5 lines after the `Build` line), zero JSON-shape impact (only the human path is touched), and existing StatusCommandTests assert presence of labels not absence of additional lines so no test break. Genuine usability win, not bikeshedding — this is the exact 'self-curing CLI' pattern doctor already follows. Side benefit: also closes a stale-doc nit (README L222 still says 'JSON snapshot' from before P15-026; can be fixed in the same diff).

title: `ContextNotSet` remediation says 'Call lacerte_set_context first' but never tells the LLM how to discover valid args
userImpact: This is the FIRST error every LLM consumer hits — open Claude Desktop, ask 'show my Lacerte clients', the LLM calls `lacerte_client_list`, the response is `ContextNotSet` with remediation `Call lacerte_set_context first.` The LLM has no signal that `lacerte_list_datapaths` is the discovery primitive, and in sim mode (the only mode that works on a dev box) `lacerte_list_datapaths` currently returns empty so the LLM has no way to construct a valid `dataPath`. Result: the LLM either fabricates a path like 'C:\Lacerte\data' and gets a second error, or it gives up and tells the user the tool is broken.
description: `SyntheticStatusCodes.StatusTable[ContextNotSet]` carries the userMessage 'A read/write tool was called before lacerte_set_context provided Datapath + TaxYear + ReturnType.' and the remediation 'Call lacerte_set_context first.' This is technically correct but operationally insufficient. Compare with `UnknownFieldAccess` (9012) which is much more actionable: it tells the operator the exact CLI command to run. The same standard should apply here: the LLM needs to know (a) the discovery primitive is `lacerte_list_datapaths`, (b) the module list is from `lacerte_list_modules`, and (c) in sim mode the canonical seeded paths.
recommendation: Tighten the remediation to: `First call lacerte_list_datapaths to discover available (path, year, module) triples (in sim mode use C:\Lacerte\{YY}Tax\{Module}Data — IData/CData/PData are seeded for TY20+TY24). Then call lacerte_set_context with the chosen triple.` Optionally also stuff the discovered datapaths into the `context` dict of the thrown error so the LLM doesn't even need a second tool call.
rationale: Round-2 error-UX lens looked at error shape consistency and origin discriminator (P15-035, P15-052) but never tested the actual first-error-an-LLM-hits remediation against the LLM tool-use loop. ContextNotSet is the load-bearing onboarding error and its remediation needs to be more than a one-liner.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all factual claims. SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:159-163 shows ContextNotSet's remediation is literally "Call lacerte_set_context first." — terse compared to siblings (UnknownFieldAccess gives a CLI command, InvalidDataPath gives a concrete path example + env-var escape hatch, LoginExpired names the re-auth command). LacerteSessionManager.cs:1319 throws with NO context dict at all, so the error payload carries no discovery signal. Critically, SessionTools.cs:141-156 (LacerteListDatapaths) only scans the local filesystem under LACERTE_DATA_ROOT/C:\Lacerte — it does NOT surface SeedData.cs's four canonical sim paths (DataPathIData2020/2024, DataPathCData2024, DataPathPData2024). Confirmed C:\Lacerte does not exist on this dev box, so on the typical operator's first session in sim mode, lacerte_list_datapaths returns count=0 and the LLM has no path to construct a valid dataPath. The intake prompt does name lacerte_list_datapaths, but the LLM won't have invoked the prompt before hitting the first lacerte_client_list call — the error remediation is the only in-band hint. Not duplicated by R1/R2 (P15-035/P15-050/P15-052 covered error-shape consistency and IsRegistered gating but never the load-bearing onboarding remediation copy or the sim-discovery gap). The "stuff seeded paths into the error context dict" addendum is the higher-leverage piece — it converts a two-error onboarding into a self-healing first error.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Two coordinated fixes, both pure-C# and sim-verifiable off-Windows:

1. **Tighten the ContextNotSet remediation string** in `src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:163`:
   ```
   "Call lacerte_list_datapaths to discover available (path, year, module) triples, then lacerte_set_context with the chosen triple. In simulation mode the canonical seeded paths are C:\\Lacerte\\20Tax\\IData (TY20 individual), C:\\Lacerte\\24Tax\\IData (TY24 individual), C:\\Lacerte\\24Tax\\CData (TY24 corp), and C:\\Lacerte\\24Tax\\PData (TY24 partnership) — module set is I/C/P/S/F/R/T/N/B via lacerte_list_modules."
   ```

2. **Make lacerte_list_datapaths sim-aware** so it self-heals the discovery gap rather than depending on the operator reading the remediation. In `SessionTools.LacerteListDatapaths` (SessionTools.cs:143-156), when the manager is in sim mode AND DiscoverDatapaths returns empty, append the four `SeedData.DataPath*` constants as synthetic entries (with a `source: "simulation-seed"` flag so the LLM can tell them apart from real filesystem hits). This requires injecting either `LacerteSessionManager` (already constructor-injected) or `SessionMode` into the discovery call and a small read against `SeedData` constants. Add a `SessionToolsTests` case asserting that in sim mode with a non-existent root, the four canonical seeded paths come back with source="simulation-seed".

3. **Stuff context into the throw** at `LacerteSessionManager.cs:1319` — change `throw new LacerteSDKError(SyntheticStatusCodes.ContextNotSet)` to pass a dict with `{ discoveryTool = "lacerte_list_datapaths", moduleList = "lacerte_list_modules", mode = Mode.ToString() }`. The WrapToolHandler envelope already plumbs the context dict to the wire so this needs no plumbing changes.

Fix #2 is the highest-value piece — it makes the dev box experience work end-to-end without requiring the LLM to have read either the README prompts table or the new remediation text. Tests pass on the existing 1006/1016 baseline because SessionToolsTests.cs:172-182 only assert "non-existent root returns empty," which would need to be updated to "non-existent root returns empty in live mode; returns seeded canonical paths in sim mode."

title: `LACERTE_DATA_PATH` listed in README env table as 'Default datapath' is misleading — it is never auto-applied to Context
userImpact: An operator setting up Claude Desktop reads the env-table row `LACERTE_DATA_PATH | live mode | Default datapath (e.g. C:\Lacerte\24data)`. They reasonably interpret this as 'set this env var and the MCP will pre-fill the session context.' They restart Claude, ask it to list clients, and get a `ContextNotSet` error anyway — because `LacerteSessionManager` only reads `LACERTE_APP_NAME` and `LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR` at construction; `LACERTE_DATA_PATH` is never consumed at startup, only quoted inside one ODBC error-message remediation. The operator's debugging journey from 'I set the env var, why doesn't it work' to 'oh you also have to call set_context every session' is a 10-minute trust-killer.
description: Grepping the server tree shows `LACERTE_DATA_PATH` consumed only at StatusCodes.cs L92 inside the `Confirm LACERTE_DATA_PATH exists` error-message string — there is no `Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("LACERTE_DATA_PATH")` read path that seeds a default `SessionContext`. The README env-table and `.env.example` (L15-17) both present it as a startup configuration, but it is purely advisory. The `doctor` command also probes it (per README L273) which further reinforces the false expectation that it is load-bearing. Additionally, the README example value `C:\Lacerte\24data` (lowercase 'data') does not match the `{Module}Data` (PascalCase) pattern that `LacerteListDatapaths` and `SeedData.DataPathIData2024 = C:\Lacerte\24Tax\IData` use — a second small inconsistency the operator must reconcile.
recommendation: Either (a) wire `LACERTE_DATA_PATH` to seed a default SessionContext at startup (paired with `LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR` + a new `LACERTE_DEFAULT_MODULE`) so the env-table promise is real — this also eliminates the need for `lacerte_set_context` on the first call when the operator pins one datapath, or (b) re-label the env-table row to `LACERTE_DATA_PATH | doctor-probe only | unset | Advisory path quoted in ODBC error remediations and probed by lacerte-mcp doctor. Not auto-applied — every session must still call lacerte_set_context.` Also fix the example value to `C:\Lacerte\24Tax\IData` to match the actual folder convention.
rationale: Round-2 config-validation lens validated env values that ARE read (P15-004 LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR fail-loud). It did not audit env vars that are documented as load-bearing but never consumed. This is a classic doc-vs-code drift the operator pays for in trust.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by direct evidence:

1. **README L91** advertises `LACERTE_DATA_PATH | live mode | unset | Default datapath (e.g. C:\Lacerte\24data)` — natural read is "set this and the MCP pre-fills the session."

2. **ARCHITECTURE.md L176** is even more explicit (and worse): `LACERTE_DATA_PATH | Default datapath if lacerte_set_context not yet called.` That sentence promises auto-fallback behavior that does not exist.

3. **LacerteSessionManager.cs** constructor (lines 220-239) reads ONLY `LACERTE_APP_NAME` and `LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR`. No `Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("LACERTE_DATA_PATH")`, no `_defaultDataPath` field, no SessionContext seeding. `Context` stays null until `SetContext(dataPath, taxYear, module, readOnly)` is called explicitly.

4. **Grep confirms** only two prod consumers: `DoctorCommand.cs:329` (probe) and `StatusCodes.cs:92` (error-message string). Tests at `DoctorCommandTests.cs:288` also reference it but only for the probe.

5. **Exact precedent**: r2 finding P15-004 fixed the identical drift for `LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR` ("documented since Phase-1 docs; before P15-004 the code never read it"). The reasoning in r2 explicitly enumerated env vars read by code and called out that `LACERTE_DATA_PATH` is read by DoctorCommand only — but the actual remediation for the sibling `LACERTE_DATA_PATH` doc-vs-code drift was never opened.

6. **Not duplicated**: Searched audit-findings.json, audit-findings-r2.json, .todo-phase14-addendum.md, .todo-phase15-addendum.md. Phase 14 fixed `LACERTE_DATAPATH` typo in StatusCodes string and added missing rows for `DATA_ROOT`/`MCP_FORCE_FILE_STORE`/`PARITY_RECORDING`. Phase 15 added probes and validated `DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR`. No prior task closes the gap between the "Default datapath" promise and the SetContext requirement.

**Operator-experience cost is real**: Tax pro reads env table, sets var, restarts Claude Desktop, gets `ContextNotSet` on first call — exactly the 10-minute trust killer the finding describes. Same shape as the P15-004 fix that was deemed worth landing.

**One weak point in the finding**: the example-value criticism (`C:\Lacerte\24data` lowercase vs `C:\Lacerte\24Tax\IData` PascalCase) misfires. `C:\Lacerte\24data` is the actual canonical Lacerte install layout — it's referenced 30+ times in REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md as the test datapath, and README L311 itself uses it. `{YY}Tax\{Module}Data` is the `LACERTE_DATA_ROOT` discovery sub-pattern, not the per-firm datapath. Drop that part of the recommendation; the core finding still stands.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Pick option (b) — re-label, don't re-architect. The "auto-seed SessionContext from env" path (option a) requires THREE coordinated env vars (`LACERTE_DATA_PATH` + `LACERTE_DEFAULT_TAX_YEAR` [already wired] + a NEW `LACERTE_DEFAULT_MODULE`) plus a `_readOnly` default, then a new code path in the ctor that calls SetContext, plus tests that the implicit context survives mode switches and Register() — meaningful surface area for a single-operator personal tool. The honest, low-risk fix:

(1) **README.md L91** — change the row to:
`| LACERTE_DATA_PATH | advisory only | unset | Quoted in ODBC-error remediations and probed by lacerte-mcp doctor. NOT auto-applied to session context — every session must still call lacerte_set_context. |`

(2) **ARCHITECTURE.md L176** — replace the misleading "Default datapath if lacerte_set_context not yet called" wording with the same advisory-only language. This line is the worst offender because it literally promises fallback behavior.

(3) **.env.example L15-17** — change the comment from "Default datapath (folder where DATA{n}{module}{YY}.DBF live for the active firm)" to "Advisory only — referenced in doctor diagnostics and ODBC error remediations. Does not auto-populate session context; every session still calls lacerte_set_context."

(4) **Leave the example value `C:\Lacerte\24data` as-is** — it matches the canonical install convention used across REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md and the README troubleshooting section.

(5) Optional sweep: confirm no other doc string (status snapshot prose, doctor warn-message remediation, etc.) implies the var seeds context. Quick `Grep "Default datapath"` already returned exactly the two doc sites; no code strings claim it.

If the operator ever asks for the auto-seed feature explicitly, file a separate follow-up that introduces `LACERTE_DEFAULT_DATA_PATH` + `LACERTE_DEFAULT_MODULE` + `LACERTE_DEFAULT_READ_ONLY` as a triple, with construction-time validation parallel to P15-004's tax-year fail-loud. But that's a feature, not a doc-drift fix; ship the doc fix now to stop new operators from burning ten minutes on a phantom contract.

title: EFileTools surfaces statusCode 9013 'InvalidDataPath' for a bad sinceUtc date — wrong code, misleading message
userImpact: When the LLM passes an unparseable date like `sinceUtc="yesterday"` or `sinceUtc="2026-13-01"`, the wire envelope returns `statusCode: 9013, statusName: "InvalidDataPath", userMessage: "lacerte_set_context rejected the dataPath — relative path, '..' traversal, control characters, UNC without LACERTE_ALLOW_UNC=1, or outside LACERTE_DATA_ROOT."`. The actual reason ('sinceUtc must be ISO-8601') is only in the context dict — the LLM will read the statusName + userMessage first, conclude the dataPath is wrong, and likely call lacerte_set_context again instead of fixing the date string. This burns one or two retries every time the LLM mis-formats the threshold.
description: EFileTools.cs:50-56 throws `new LacerteSDKError(SyntheticStatusCodes.InvalidDataPath, ...)` for a date parse failure. InvalidDataPath (9013) is exclusively about path validation everywhere else (BridgeInputValidation.cs:160/171/184, PathValidation.cs:259, LacerteSessionManager.cs:520). Its canonical userMessage/remediation in SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:171-175 talks about UNC paths and LACERTE_DATA_ROOT — completely unrelated to date parsing. There is no existing synthetic code for 'bad argument format'; the closest neighbors are 9009 InvalidContext and 9011 InvalidModule.
recommendation: Either (a) introduce a new synthetic code like `InvalidArgument = 9018` with userMessage 'Tool argument failed validation' and remediation 'See context.reason for the specific argument that failed', then use it here and audit other call sites that abuse InvalidDataPath the same way; or (b) cheaper one-line fix — throw a more semantic existing code (e.g. reuse `FieldWriteInvalid` is wrong too; honestly the cleanest is option a). The new-code option is ~10 lines and removes a class of message confusion. Either way, also tighten the EFileTools description string to say `sinceUtc` is treated as date-only at UTC 00:00 (today it implies the time can be set but the parsing array discards everything else for the date comparison anyway).
rationale: Not flagged in R1/R2 (their error-message-ux passes covered status mapping in general but not this specific mis-mapping). Concrete user-visible: every LLM hitting a sinceUtc parse error gets a message about dataPath. Low fix cost, high readability win.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified directly: EFileTools.cs:50-56 throws LacerteSDKError(SyntheticStatusCodes.InvalidDataPath=9013) for `sinceUtc` ISO-8601 parse failure. The 9013 StatusInfo entry at SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:171-175 has userMessage 'lacerte_set_context rejected the dataPath — relative path, ".." traversal, control characters, UNC without LACERTE_ALLOW_UNC=1, or outside LACERTE_DATA_ROOT' and remediation 'Pass an absolute local path under the Lacerte install root (e.g. C:\\Lacerte\\24Tax\\IData). Set LACERTE_ALLOW_UNC=1 to permit \\\\server\\share paths.' Both are entirely about path validation — completely wrong for a date parse error. WrapToolHandler.SerializeError stamps statusName, userMessage, and remediation directly on the wire envelope (lines 144-157), so the LLM sees three top-level fields screaming "path problem" plus a context.reason whispering "date problem." Real LLM behavior will trust the more prominent fields and rerun lacerte_set_context, burning 1-2 retries.

The 8 other InvalidDataPath call sites (BridgeInputValidation.cs:160/171/184, PathValidation.cs:259, plus session manager comments) are all path-related — so the message IS accurate everywhere else, just wrong in EFileTools.

This is a new finding generated by the R2 P15-010 fix landing with the wrong code. P15-010's refinedRecommendation explicitly said to use a new `SyntheticStatusCodes.InvalidArgument` code, but implementation took a shortcut and reused 9013. EFileToolsTests.cs:85-87 even has a comment defending the reuse ("operator-actionable, no need for a fresh code") — that comment will be the regression-guard test that has to flip alongside the fix.

Fix is genuinely cheap (~10 LOC for a new SyntheticStatusCodes.InvalidArgument=9018 with a generic 'Tool argument failed validation; see context.reason for the specific argument' userMessage + remediation) and removes a clearly misleading wire message. Future tools doing per-arg validation (the WrapToolHandler refactor or any new tool with optional filters) will reuse the new code instead of repeating the InvalidDataPath misuse. Meaningfully improves LLM retry behavior — not bikeshedding.

The secondary tightening the finding suggests (clarifying sinceUtc is treated as a date-only at UTC 00:00) is a minor doc tweak with smaller payoff but lives in the same one-line touch — worth keeping in the recommendation.

title: `stateAbbrev` vs `stateAbbr` — same concept, two parameter names across the tool surface
userImpact: An LLM that just used `lacerte_table_read(stateAbbrev="CA")` and then tries `lacerte_detail_write(stateAbbrev="CA", ...)` gets an unknown-parameter rejection — `LacerteDetailWrite` calls it `stateAbbr`. The model then has to retry, which wastes a tool turn and erodes trust. This is exactly the kind of trivial inconsistency that makes the API feel slapped together.
description: `DetailsTools.LacerteDetailWrite` uses `[Description("State abbreviation...")] string stateAbbr,` (DetailsTools.cs:108). Every other tool — `LacerteTableRead`, `LacerteStateRead`, `LacerteStateSubclientRead`, `LacerteFieldWrite`, `LacerteUpdateReturn`, and the `BulkWriteEntry.StateAbbrev` field — uses `stateAbbrev`. The DBF column itself is `StateAbbrev`, so `stateAbbr` is the outlier.
recommendation: Rename the DetailWrite parameter to `stateAbbrev` (and the internal `_rxStateAbbr` regex variable for clarity). Update DetailsTools.cs:108, 127, 134, 157, 201, 207, 208 plus any test references. The `DetailRow` record's `StateAbbr` member can keep that name internally — it's not on the MCP wire — or rename it too to flush the inconsistency. The tool param name is the only on-wire token an LLM sees.
rationale: Not surfaced in either prior round; both rounds focused on response shape, validation logic, and architectural issues but did not audit cross-tool parameter naming consistency.

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly: DetailsTools.cs:108 declares `string stateAbbr` while every other MCP-wire tool — FieldWriteTools.cs:48, UpdateReturnTools.cs:59, TablesTools.cs:27, StatesTools.cs:24 and :41, FieldWriteBulkTools.cs:73 (BulkWriteEntry.StateAbbrev) — uses `stateAbbrev`. The underlying DBF column is `StateAbbrev`, so `stateAbbr` on `lacerte_detail_write` is the sole outlier on the entire wire surface. Confirmed against audit-findings.json (71 entries) and audit-findings-r2.json (78 entries): both rounds covered detail-row validation (P14-002), DBF column type alignment for Series/Code, and ValidateDetailWrite shape gates, but no entry ever flagged the parameter-name asymmetry that the LLM sees on the wire. The user impact is real for the operator profile: an LLM driving Claude Desktop / Cursor / Windsurf almost always learns parameter conventions from one tool and reuses them on the next — sending `stateAbbrev` to `lacerte_detail_write` will get rejected by MCP JSON-RPC parameter validation, costing a full tool round-trip and surfacing as a cryptic "unknown parameter" error in the operator's transcript. Fix is small and contained (rename param at DetailsTools.cs:108, propagate to lines 127/134/157/201/207/208 and the private `_rxStateAbbr` regex name; the DetailRow record's `StateAbbr` member is internal and can stay or be renamed for hygiene). This is exactly the cross-tool-inconsistency Round 3 is hunting for.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Rename the on-wire parameter on `DetailsTools.LacerteDetailWrite` from `stateAbbr` to `stateAbbrev` at DetailsTools.cs:108, and follow through on the internal references that need updating: line 127 (`ValidateDetailWrite(series, code, stateAbbr, tsj)` call), line 134 (`StateAbbr: stateAbbr ?? ""` in DetailRow construction — record member stays `StateAbbr` since it's internal), line 157 (`ValidateDetailWrite` signature parameter), lines 201/207/208 (the regex match + the error-context `field`/`value` keys — note: the `field` and `reason` strings inside the LacerteSDKError context should switch to "stateAbbrev" + "StateAbbrev must be empty OR a 2-letter uppercase postal code" so the error matches what the operator passed). Optionally rename the `_rxStateAbbr` regex variable to `_rxStateAbbrev` to flush the inconsistency at the call site. Leave the `DetailRow` record's `StateAbbr` property name as-is (it's internal model, not on the wire) — renaming it would ripple into Writer.cs, SimulationStore detail handling, and seed fixtures with no user-visible benefit. Update DetailsToolsTests.cs to the new parameter name. Verify `dotnet build` is clean and the existing detail-write tests still pass. The on-wire token an LLM sees is the only thing that needs to change.

title: `LacerteUpdateReturn` description says it's 'Equivalent surface to lacerte_field_write' — gives LLM no decision criteria, invites coin-flips
userImpact: When two tools have identical inputs and the description literally says 'Equivalent surface', the LLM picks at random — sometimes `lacerte_field_write`, sometimes `lacerte_update_return`, often within the same session for the same client. That randomness shows up in tool-call traces and confuses operators reading logs, and it makes prompt-engineered tool-list snippets in docs fight each other ('always use field_write' vs 'always use update_return for TY21+').
description: Description text: 'TY21+ explicit write entrypoint (UpdateTaxReturn under the hood, keyed by ClientNumber). Equivalent surface to lacerte_field_write — both go through the same session chokepoint which year-routes the backend call. Use this when you specifically want the TY21+ API in a TY21+ context.' Since the session year-routes either way, 'specifically want' is a distinction with no behavioral consequence to the operator. The XML comment above admits 'the model gets a clearer surface this way' — but on the wire the model just sees two indistinguishable choices.
recommendation: Either (a) collapse to one tool (`lacerte_field_write`) and delete `lacerte_update_return` — round-1 finding P14-051 already flagged consolidation; the surface dedup is the user-facing version. Or (b) rewrite the description to be unambiguous about when to NOT use it: 'Prefer lacerte_field_write — this tool is an alias kept for parity with the Lacerte SDK developer docs. If you have no specific reason, do not use this tool.' That actively steers the LLM away from the duplicate.
rationale: Round 1 P14-051 flagged the *code* duplication and round 1 P14-026 fixed the misleading `api=` field. Neither addressed the LLM-facing tool-selection ambiguity that the redundant tool *still creates*. This is purely a usability framing issue.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by reading both tool files directly. UpdateReturnTools.cs:52 description literally says "Equivalent surface to lacerte_field_write" and "Use this when you specifically want the TY21+ API in a TY21+ context" — but since the session manager year-routes either tool to the right wire call, "specifically want" has no observable behavioral consequence. FieldWriteTools.cs:41 description is the mirror image ("use lacerte_update_return for an explicit entrypoint"), so both tools point at each other with no decision criteria. The XML doc-comment in UpdateReturnTools.cs:20 explicitly admits the design depends on "the model gets a clearer surface this way" — but the surface the model actually sees (the [Description] attribute) gives it no clarity, just a coin-flip pointer to its sibling.

Prior audit cross-check: P14-051 (round 1, lines 1103-1121 of audit-findings.json) addressed only the CODE duplication via a shared FieldWriteCore.Run helper — confirmed already landed; both tools now delegate to it identically. The reasoning on that ticket explicitly says "Both tools can keep their distinct [McpServerTool] attributes for model-clarity" — i.e., the round-1 decision was to keep both tools and rely on description text to disambiguate, but the description text was never sharpened to actually do that work. P14-026 fixed the misleading `api="UpdateTaxReturn"` envelope field, also did not touch descriptions. No round-2 ticket addresses the LLM-facing description ambiguity. So the finding is genuinely new and slots between two prior tickets that each touched adjacent issues without closing this one.

Why meaningfullyImproves=true: Operators reading Claude Desktop / Cursor tool-call traces will see the same LLM oscillate between `lacerte_field_write` and `lacerte_update_return` for the same TY24 client in the same session — exactly the kind of "feels slapped together" signal that erodes trust in the MCP surface. The model also wastes tokens reasoning about which alias to pick. Cost to fix: a one-line description edit on each file. Round-3-shaped finding (LLM picking-friction, polish, post-149-ticket gap).
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Two coordinated one-line description edits — keep both tools (P14-051 already committed to that for SDK-docs parity), but make the [Description] attributes actually steer the LLM instead of bouncing it between aliases.

1) UpdateReturnTools.cs:52 — replace the current Description with: `"Alias for lacerte_field_write kept to mirror Intuit's TY21+ UpdateTaxReturn developer-doc surface. Behavior is identical: both funnel through the same session chokepoint and the session year-routes the backend call. Prefer lacerte_field_write in new code — only use this tool when a user prompt or workflow explicitly references the UpdateTaxReturn SDK API by name. Returns the TAPIStatus integer (1=Success)."`

2) FieldWriteTools.cs:41 — replace the current Description with: `"Write a single field value to a DATA1..DATA5 row for the active context (DATA6/DATA7 are read-only per spec). Pre-TY21 contexts use WriteToDBFDatabase; TY21+ contexts route to UpdateTaxReturn — both transparently, no caller branching needed. This is the primary write entrypoint for all years; lacerte_update_return is a thin alias retained for SDK-docs parity. Returns the TAPIStatus integer (1=Success)."`

Key shifts: (a) drop the "Equivalent surface" phrasing — replaces a symmetric pointer with an asymmetric "prefer X" steer; (b) explicit "Alias" wording on the update_return side gives the LLM a tie-breaker; (c) field_write description stops naming update_return as an "explicit entrypoint" (which currently reads as an upgrade path) and instead positions it as the secondary; (d) the SDK-docs-parity rationale is now visible to the model rather than hidden in the C# /// comment, so a curious model has a reason to leave update_return alone rather than treat it as the "specialized" choice.

Also update the corresponding /// <summary> blocks for code-reading humans to use the same "alias / primary" framing instead of the current "we exposed two MCP tools for clarity" language, which justifies keeping both but does not tell the model how to choose.

No test changes required (existing UpdateReturnToolsTests still pass — they hit behavior, not description text). Consider adding a single sanity test in WorkflowPromptsTests or a new MetadataConsistencyTests that asserts the substring "Alias for lacerte_field_write" appears in update_return's description and "primary write entrypoint" appears in field_write's — locks the steer against future drift.

title: Sub-resource tools (subclients/states/status/forms) read entire client without limit — large clients blow MCP message budget
userImpact: A partnership with 200 partners triggers `lacerte_subclient_read(clientNumber=...)` returning all 200 DATA2 rows in one envelope. An LLM with a 25k-token result window then has to summarize without paging. The model often produces a half-summary, hits the truncation cliff, and emits 'I'll continue with the rest' which never happens. Round 2 noted this for EF status / details / forms generically; the per-entity sub-resource tools are the *common* path and were not all fixed.
description: Round 2 finding 'Six read tools return unbounded result sets' was scoped to detail/EF/forms. `LacerteSubclientRead`, `LacerteStateRead`, `LacerteStateSubclientRead`, and `LacerteStatusRead` still return `{ clientNumber, count, subclients }`-shape envelopes with no `limit`/`offset` parameters. Test the partnership case: each partner has C2 fields plus possibly dozens of per-partner state rows via DATA4 — the unfiltered DATA4 read for a 50-state 200-partner return is 10,000 rows.
recommendation: Add the same `limit`/`offset` parameters and `{ rows, total, limit, offset, hasMore, nextOffset }` envelope already on the other paginated tools. Reuse `Pagination.Page<T>` so the contract is identical. Once landed, every read tool in the project paginates the same way — a single fact the LLM can carry across all 14 reads.
rationale: Round 2 'Six read tools return unbounded result sets' covered the principle for EF/detail/forms but the per-resource subclients/states/status tools are still unpaginated. This is the same finding extended to the tools that were missed; flagged because the prior fix was incomplete.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by reading all five cited tool files plus the canonical paginated examples. Findings:

(1) ABSOLUTE confirmation of the gap: SubclientsTools.cs:23-34 returns `{clientNumber, count, subclients=rows}` with zero limit/offset; StatesTools.cs:22-52 same shape for both LacerteStateRead AND LacerteStateSubclientRead; StatusTools.cs:23-34 returns `{clientNumber, count, statuses=rows}`; FormsTools.cs:22-33 returns `{clientNumber, count, forms=rows}`. None of them have any pagination parameter.

(2) The finding actually UNDERSTATES the gap — EFileTools.cs:34-62 (LacerteEfStatus) is also unpaginated: returns `{count, efStatuses=rows}` with no limit/offset. Per P15-047's own refined recommendation in audit-findings-r2.json line 1141, EFStatus was ranked the HIGHEST priority of all six tools because of the module-wide join with no client filter. It was missed entirely.

(3) Critical inconsistency between docs and reality: Todo.md line 701 marks P15-047 `[x]` complete with the recommendation calling out all six tools by name (Detail, EFStatus, Subclient, StateRead, StateSubclientRead, Forms, Status). Only DetailsTools was actually updated. The other five tools — including the highest-priority EFStatus — were skipped despite the task being checked off. The .todo-phase15-addendum.md line 203 still shows `[ ]` (unchecked), confirming the task was prematurely marked done in Todo.md.

(4) Real usability impact: A tax-pro firm running `lacerte_ef_status` (no client filter) at peak season (200+ EF filings across the practice) will receive an unbounded JSON envelope. The LLM (Claude Desktop ~25k token result window) truncates, summarizes partially, and the operator gets a "let me continue with the rest" that never happens. Same for a 200-partner partnership returning all subclients. Add a 50-state apportionment and DATA4 emits up to 10,000 rows in one envelope.

(5) Cross-tool inconsistency hurts the LLM more than the operator: when 3 of 8 read tools paginate and 5 don't, the LLM has no consistent rule to apply. The whole point of P15-047 was uniformity ("a single fact the LLM can carry across all 14 reads"); leaving the work half-done is worse than not starting because it creates the illusion of consistency.
